articles.title: Phyllida Law: Actress who starred with daughters Emma and Sophie Thompson dies
articles.summary: Law appeared in films alongside both of her daughters, Dame Emma and Sophie, including 1996's Emma.
articles.body:
Stage and screen star Phyllida Law, the mother of fellow actresses Dame Emma and Sophie Thompson, has died at the age of 94.

"It is with great sadness we have to announce that Phyllida Law died supremely peacefully at home, surrounded by all of her family, on Monday 27th July," her manager Jacky Leggo said in a statement to BBC News.

"We had worked together for over fifty years and she was a beautiful person inside and out."

Law appeared on screen alongside her daughters several times throughout a long and varied career, including in the 1996 adaptation of Jane Austen's Emma, starring Gwyneth Paltrow. Law played Mrs Bates while Sophie played her daughter Miss Bates.

She also acted with Dame Emma in 1992's Peter's Friends, directed by her then-son-in-law Sir Kenneth Branagh.

They combined on screen again the following year in Sir Kenneth's adaptation of William Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.

And they played a mother and daughter in Alan Rickman's directorial debut, The Winter Guest, in 1997.

Later in life, Law provided the voice of Mrs Partridge in Dame Emma's 2005 film Nanny McPhee, which her eldest daughter wrote and starred in.

'They didn't follow in our footsteps, they rushed past us'

Born in Glasgow in 1932, Law attended the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, initially to become a stage designer but ended up studying acting instead "by happy accident".

She married fellow actor Eric Thompson - best known for The Magic Roundabout - in 1957.

The couple were together until he died of a heart attack aged 53, in 1982.

Throughout a career spanning eight decades, Law would go on to appear in numerous TV shows including Dixon of Dock Green and Rumpole of the Bailey before Midsomer Murders, Foyle's War, Doc Martin and New Tricks.

She was also known for her work on the big screen in films such as Anna Karenina, Saving Grace and Miss Potter.

On stage, Law appeared alongside Alec Guinness in John Mortimer's A Voyage Round My Father in London's West End in 1971, and in Alan Bennett's Habeas Corpus at the Oxford Playhouse in 1973, which then transferred to the capital.

She also played Jacqueline in the original London cast of La Cage Aux Folles at the London Palladium in 1986.

The prolific character actress starred alongside John Hurt in a short film entitled Love at First Sight which was shortlisted for an Oscar in 2012.

Law received an OBE in 2014 for services to drama and for charitable services.

Her daughters have both gone on to enjoy success on screen.

Emma was born in 1959 and has won two Oscars - one for acting in Howard's End and another for writing the screenplay for Sense and Sensibility - and is also known for featuring in Love Actually and the Harry Potter film series.

Sophie was born in 1964 and has appeared in films including Gosford Park and Four Weddings and a Funeral, and been nominated for seven Olivier Awards on stage.

Speaking about her daughters to the Telegraph in 2017 , Law said: "They are both my colleagues in a way. They didn't follow in our footsteps, they rushed past us, trampling on us."

The family acting dynasty has continued with Dame Emma's daughter Gaia, who posted on Instagram about her grandmother: "Rest well my queen."

Speaking of her love of the arts to the same newspaper, Law joked: "I've got to have my funeral in the afternoon, curtain up 2.30pm, so people can get to the theatre afterwards."

I'll wear it to bed, says Emma Thompson after award win at Hay Festival

Emma Thompson's love for her first edition Jane Austen

articles.title: Fantasy Football: 7 players Justin Boone thinks could be league winners in 2026
articles.summary: These players could define the 2026 fantasy football season.
articles.body:
Identifying the players who could define the fantasy season is one of my favorite exercises to do each year. While it's unlikely you'll be able to draft all the names on this list, building your roster around even a few of these players can significantly increase your odds of reaching the fantasy playoffs and hopefully bringing home the championship.

When it became obvious earlier this offseason that A.J. Brown's time with the Eagles was coming to an end, I didn't expect to be as interested in Hurts for fantasy. Usually, it's a bad omen when a quarterback loses their top receiver. However, the more I dug into Hurts' outlook moving forward, the more optimistic it turned out to be.

Even in a down season last year, Hurts still finished as the QB8 in fantasy points per game. That makes it five consecutive campaigns inside the top eight at his position, including finishes as the QB6, QB2, QB1 and QB7 overall.

While Hurts isn't without blame for Philly's struggles a year ago, we can easily point to former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo's stagnant scheme as a big part of the problem. Enter new OC Sean Mannion, who will modernize their attack with more pre-snap motion and play-action. He's also challenging Hurts to evolve his game and take more chances downfield.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

To do that, Hurts will need time in the pocket. Another factor that held the Eagles back last season was the health of their offensive line. Better injury luck is never guaranteed, but we can be hopeful their starters don't deal with as many ailments this time around. Brandon Thorn of Establish the Run ranked this group as the second best set of blockers in the league.

Replacing Brown in the passing game won't be easy, but DeVonta Smith has long been an overqualified No. 2 receiver. (Spoiler: we'll discuss him more a little further down this list.)

First-round wideout Makai Lemon has missed significant time with a hamstring injury, so his impact may not be truly felt until partway through the season. Fortunately, Dontayvion Wicks has stepped up and appears to be ready for a meaningful role with his new club. That doesn't even account for superstar back Saquon Barkley and stalwart tight end Dallas Goedert.

If you're still not convinced, know that Hurts will encounter the easiest fantasy schedule of any quarterback — a major improvement from what he faced last year.

Thanks to all the talented fantasy options among quarterbacks this season, Hurts is going off the board as the QB6 near the Round 5-6 turn. I've even seen him fall to the seventh round in some of my redraft leagues this month. That's incredible value for a player who always has the potential for a transcendent season — aided by his tush-push-inflated TD scoring.

Some of my favorite builds this summer have involved me drafting two running backs, two receivers and a tight end in the first five rounds, before grabbing Hurts in the sixth or seventh.

Taylor represents a very specific range in drafts, since he's almost always gone inside the top seven selections of the first round. It's an area where you want to come away with a player who can be the anchor of your fantasy lineup and we saw JT accomplish that feat last season.

While he ended the year as the second-highest scoring running back (20.9 fppg) behind only Christian McCaffrey, that included the games where Philip Rivers and Riley Leonard had to step in for an injured Daniel Jones down the stretch.

Before Jones got hurt, Taylor was the RB1 overall with 23 fppg in half PPR — ahead of CMC — through the first 13 weeks. He was also averaging 104 rushing yards per contest during that span. With Jones on the field the Colts were No. 1 in yards per play, EPA per play, success rate and points per drive. After his injury they failed to win a game and fell to 18th or worse in all those categories. Taylor dropped to just 57 yards per outing.

Even if Jones isn't 100% back to form for Week 1, having him under center will be a big boost to the offense. With him, Taylor can challenge for elite status among fantasy RBs as he goes up against the seventh easiest collection of opponents for his position in 2026, while running behind an offensive line the aforementioned Brandon Thorn ranked sixth best league-wide.

It's also safe to wonder if we could witness another career high in receptions for Taylor, after he posted 46 last year. With Michael Pittman Jr. gone and Alec Pierce dealing with an ankle injury that could sideline him at the beginning of the season, Taylor might be relied upon even more as a pass-catcher.

Few players have the talent and volume to compete for the fantasy RB crown, but Taylor is among them.

Walker occupied this same space last year and began the season with two top-10 weekly RB finishes in the first three weeks, but ultimately spent most of the season splitting time with Zach Charbonnet. The Seahawks' decision to split backfield touches turned out to be the right one because it kept Walker fresh for a late-season run that helped them win the Super Bowl.

Over Walker's final six games (including three playoff contests), he averaged 128.5 scrimmage yards and nearly a touchdown per appearance. Those numbers were amplified by Charbonnet suffering a torn ACL in the postseason, but Walker's hot streak had already begun by that point. It eventually culminated in taking home the Super Bowl MVP award.

Though that hindsight analysis can't change our 2025 fantasy results, there's plenty of reason to get excited about Walker's potential this season.

Walker ended up in one of the ideal landing spots for a running back, joining a Chiefs offense that's been in desperate need of a playmaker who could elevate its ground attack.

The 25-year-old (turns 26 in October) is finally escaping the timeshare backfield in Seattle and won't face anywhere near the same competition for touches in Kansas City. By all accounts the Chiefs want to deploy Walker as a workhorse and help take some of the pressure off their passing attack.

While I don't expect him to ever catch enough passes to flirt with an elite season-long finish at his position, this move definitely puts him in consideration as a top-five fantasy RB — as long as he can stay healthy.

Whether it's Walker, Chase Brown or Omarion Hampton, the running backs in the second round of fantasy drafts offer tremendous value this year.

Smith has played in A.J. Brown's shadow for a long time, so it's nice to see him getting an opportunity to prove he can be a No. 1 receiver in the NFL.

Fortunately, we've been given a glimpse of what that might look like already. Over the last two seasons, there have been three games where Brown was sidelined and Smith played a full complement of snaps. The results were stat lines of 6-84-0, 7-79-0 and 7-76-1 while averaging just under 10 targets per game.

It's not like Smith has been invisible with Brown on the field. Smith was the WR17 (2024), WR21 (2023) and WR16 (2022) on a per game basis, before this past season when he finished as the WR33 amid some overall struggles in the Eagles' offense.

As I outlined in Jalen Hurts' section, there are plenty of signs pointing to the Eagles having a bounce-back campaign, including their new coordinator, some better offensive health and a very soft schedule. Like Hurts, Smith also will enjoy the easiest slate at his position in 2026.

The 27-year-old (turns 28 in November) is more than capable of shining in a bigger role and with Makai Lemon battling hamstring issues, there won't be anyone around to challenge him for the top spot.

Don't be surprised when Smith finishes as a low-end fantasy WR1 this season.

The annual tradition of trying to uncover this season's version of last year's meaningful fantasy stars can often lead managers astray as they attempt to force comparisons.

However, this year we definitely have a clear candidate to be this season's George Pickens — and that's Waddle.

Pickens was a talented receiver who flashed high-end skills in a low-volume Steelers' passing attack with questionable quarterback play. Then he joined the Cowboys high-volume pass game, where he instantly got an upgrade at QB in Dak Prescott. Though a CeeDee Lamb injury certainly helped his fantasy cause, Pickens finished as the WR6 in fppg in his debut season in Dallas.

Now consider Waddle's situation. It's been a couple seasons since he was a true impact fantasy starter, but he still managed WR28 stats on a struggling Dolphins team last year.

If you look back to the early part of his career in Miami, Waddle produced over 1,000 yards in each of his first three campaigns, resulting in fantasy finishes of WR17, WR11 and WR22.

First-rounder Travis Hunter was injured midseason and now projects to be a part-time offensive weapon while taking on a larger role on defense.

Normally, my approach to drafting a fantasy tight end involves grabbing an elite option or waiting to find a value much later. However, I've made an exception when it comes to Warren because he's an elite fantasy TE whom you can get one, two or sometimes three rounds later than the top trio at the position.

As a rookie, Warren broke onto the fantasy scene as the TE6 in per game scoring through Week 10, before he dealt with injuries down the stretch and lost his starting quarterback Daniel Jones.

On the season, Warren led the team in targets with 112, one more than teammate Michael Pittman Jr., who joined the Steelers this offseason. Alec Pierce's recovery from ankle surgery is ongoing and might result in him missing time at the start of the season. Even when Pierce is active, he's far from a target hog.

Josh Downs and Keenan Allen will benefit from the situation as well, but there's a real opportunity for the sophomore tight end to dominate targets on the Colts this year.

Jones is back and looking ready to start in Week 1. Whether he maintains his mobility coming off a torn Achilles is another question and could lead to more quick passing to the short-to-intermediate ranges of the field, where Warren excels.

His yards after the catch ability is also worth noting. Warren was second among all tight ends in total yards after the catch behind only Trey McBride. Warren was 13th in the league in YAC among all positions.

The 24-year-old's fantasy numbers can even be boosted by occasional deployment from the backfield. That was part of his game in college and he earned six carries last season, even scoring a touchdown on the ground.

Warren has a lot of the things we're looking for in an elite fantasy tight end, especially the potential to lead his team in targets and add value after the catch. Consider him Brock Bowers-lite, with an outside chance to compete for the TE1 overall throne.
paragraphs: Identifying the players who could define the fantasy season is one of my favorite exercises to do each year. While it's unlikely you'll be able to draft all the names on this list, building your roster around even a few of these players can significantly increase your odds of reaching the fantasy playoffs and hopefully bringing home the championship.

When it became obvious earlier this offseason that A.J. Brown's time with the Eagles was coming to an end, I didn't expect to be as interested in Hurts for fantasy. Usually, it's a bad omen when a quarterback loses their top receiver. However, the more I dug into Hurts' outlook moving forward, the more optimistic it turned out to be.

Even in a down season last year, Hurts still finished as the QB8 in fantasy points per game. That makes it five consecutive campaigns inside the top eight at his position, including finishes as the QB6, QB2, QB1 and QB7 overall.

While Hurts isn't without blame for Philly's struggles a year ago, we can easily point to former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo's stagnant scheme as a big part of the problem. Enter new OC Sean Mannion, who will modernize their attack with more pre-snap motion and play-action. He's also challenging Hurts to evolve his game and take more chances downfield.
Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

To do that, Hurts will need time in the pocket. Another factor that held the Eagles back last season was the health of their offensive line. Better injury luck is never guaranteed, but we can be hopeful their starters don't deal with as many ailments this time around. Brandon Thorn of Establish the Run ranked this group as the second best set of blockers in the league.
Replacing Brown in the passing game won't be easy, but DeVonta Smith has long been an overqualified No. 2 receiver. (Spoiler: we'll discuss him more a little further down this list.)

First-round wideout Makai Lemon has missed significant time with a hamstring injury, so his impact may not be truly felt until partway through the season. Fortunately, Dontayvion Wicks has stepped up and appears to be ready for a meaningful role with his new club. That doesn't even account for superstar back Saquon Barkley and stalwart tight end Dallas Goedert.
If you're still not convinced, know that Hurts will encounter the easiest fantasy schedule of any quarterback — a major improvement from what he faced last year.

Thanks to all the talented fantasy options among quarterbacks this season, Hurts is going off the board as the QB6 near the Round 5-6 turn. I've even seen him fall to the seventh round in some of my redraft leagues this month. That's incredible value for a player who always has the potential for a transcendent season — aided by his tush-push-inflated TD scoring.
Some of my favorite builds this summer have involved me drafting two running backs, two receivers and a tight end in the first five rounds, before grabbing Hurts in the sixth or seventh.

Taylor represents a very specific range in drafts, since he's almost always gone inside the top seven selections of the first round. It's an area where you want to come away with a player who can be the anchor of your fantasy lineup and we saw JT accomplish that feat last season.

While he ended the year as the second-highest scoring running back (20.9 fppg) behind only Christian McCaffrey, that included the games where Philip Rivers and Riley Leonard had to step in for an injured Daniel Jones down the stretch.

Before Jones got hurt, Taylor was the RB1 overall with 23 fppg in half PPR — ahead of CMC — through the first 13 weeks. He was also averaging 104 rushing yards per contest during that span. With Jones on the field the Colts were No. 1 in yards per play, EPA per play, success rate and points per drive. After his injury they failed to win a game and fell to 18th or worse in all those categories. Taylor dropped to just 57 yards per outing.

Even if Jones isn't 100% back to form for Week 1, having him under center will be a big boost to the offense. With him, Taylor can challenge for elite status among fantasy RBs as he goes up against the seventh easiest collection of opponents for his position in 2026, while running behind an offensive line the aforementioned Brandon Thorn ranked sixth best league-wide.

It's also safe to wonder if we could witness another career high in receptions for Taylor, after he posted 46 last year. With Michael Pittman Jr. gone and Alec Pierce dealing with an ankle injury that could sideline him at the beginning of the season, Taylor might be relied upon even more as a pass-catcher.
Few players have the talent and volume to compete for the fantasy RB crown, but Taylor is among them.

Walker occupied this same space last year and began the season with two top-10 weekly RB finishes in the first three weeks, but ultimately spent most of the season splitting time with Zach Charbonnet. The Seahawks' decision to split backfield touches turned out to be the right one because it kept Walker fresh for a late-season run that helped them win the Super Bowl.

Over Walker's final six games (including three playoff contests), he averaged 128.5 scrimmage yards and nearly a touchdown per appearance. Those numbers were amplified by Charbonnet suffering a torn ACL in the postseason, but Walker's hot streak had already begun by that point. It eventually culminated in taking home the Super Bowl MVP award.
Though that hindsight analysis can't change our 2025 fantasy results, there's plenty of reason to get excited about Walker's potential this season.
Walker ended up in one of the ideal landing spots for a running back, joining a Chiefs offense that's been in desperate need of a playmaker who could elevate its ground attack.

The 25-year-old (turns 26 in October) is finally escaping the timeshare backfield in Seattle and won't face anywhere near the same competition for touches in Kansas City. By all accounts the Chiefs want to deploy Walker as a workhorse and help take some of the pressure off their passing attack.

While I don't expect him to ever catch enough passes to flirt with an elite season-long finish at his position, this move definitely puts him in consideration as a top-five fantasy RB — as long as he can stay healthy.
Whether it's Walker, Chase Brown or Omarion Hampton, the running backs in the second round of fantasy drafts offer tremendous value this year.

Fortunately, we've been given a glimpse of what that might look like already. The results were stat lines of 6-84-0, 7-79-0 and 7-76-1 while averaging just under 10 targets per game.

articles.title: 118-year-old mystery cracked as divers discover lost warship beneath the waves
articles.summary: The wreck of HMS Tiger was found off the Isle of Wight after divers spent five years researching archives to pinpoint the Royal Navy warship lost in 1908.
articles.body: Divers recently uncovered the remains of a Royal Navy warship off the Isle of Wight — 118 years after it went down. The ship, HMS Tiger, sank in 1908 after colliding with another Royal Navy warship, the 10,000-ton HMS Berwick, news agency SWNS reported. More than half of HMS Tiger's 57 crew members were killed in the sinking. The wreck remained undiscovered until Aug. 10, when the ProjectXplore dive group announced its discovery. WRECK OF DEADLIEST US NAVAL LOSS OF WORLD WAR I FOUND AFTER MORE THAN A CENTURY: 'LOST WITH ALL HANDS' The ProjectXplore team spent five years going through archives and piecing together data that helped pinpoint the wreck's location. Images show divers exploring the twisted and rusting remains of HMS Tiger on the seabed over a century after it sank. A wreath was also laid on the wreck in memory of those who died. In a statement, the organizers of ProjectXplore called it "the privilege of a lifetime to research, discover and document the wreck of HMS Tiger." BOY STUMBLES ON STRANGE BEACH OBJECT IDENTIFIED AS RARE 1.8M-YEAR-OLD FOSSIL "We sincerely hope that our work will ensure that HMS Tiger, her story and the memory of those connected with her endure for future generations," organizers Leo Fielding and Dan McMullen said. The discovery comes as the British government moves to strengthen legal protections for military shipwrecks through its Armed Forces Bill. Under the proposed changes, wrecks such as HMS Tiger would be protected from the moment they're discovered, making it illegal to disturb the sites or remove items without permission. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Divers would still be allowed to visit under a "look but don't touch" approach. "This Armed Forces Bill is wide-ranging in the measures it proposes – from protecting our rich cultural heritage, to transforming the lives of military families by upgrading and improving the Defence housing estate," Armed Forces Minister Louise Sandher-Jones said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "These protections go further to ensure that these vulnerable and nationally significant monuments are protected from day one of discovery, giving lost sailors the dignity and respect they deserve." HMS Tiger is the latest in a series of historic shipwrecks to be discovered or documented in British waters in recent years. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Last summer, divers documented the remarkably preserved wreck of the British warship Northumberland off the coast of Kent, more than 320 years after it sank during the Great Storm of 1703. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Earlier this year, the remains of a 17th-century merchant ship believed to be The Fame, which sank in 1631, resurfaced on a beach in southwestern England after winter storms exposed the wreck.

articles.title: Millennials have found it hard to buy homes – but things may be turning a corner
articles.summary: Twenty-somethings are much less likely to own a home than previous generations. But data suggests things may be improving.
articles.body:
Leaving education, getting a job, buying a home and perhaps starting a family: the path previous generations followed may seem a distant dream to many now.

But is it getting a bit easier - at least when it comes to getting on the housing ladder?

Today's prospective first-time buyers may well feel hard done by; they are still worse off than recent generations.

If you were born in the UK in the mid-1990s you've about a 25% chance of owning your own home, as this chart shows.

Twenty-somethings in the 1990s were almost twice as likely to be on the housing ladder, the previous generation even more so.

But before looking at the current picture, what's behind the longer term shift?

One issue is that property prices have outpaced incomes across many decades.

In the chart below, housing economist Paul Cheshire puts it starkly, comparing the rise in egg prices with house prices over the past 71 years.

Changes in the mortgage markets have contributed, but ultimately it's about a lack of housebuilding.

The government previously estimated that England alone needs another 300,000 dwellings per year to keep up with population change and our preference for living in smaller households.

But only 208,000 were added last year. We've not built close to 300,000 new homes in a year for at least three decades.

There are many reasons why, but inflation has been key - from the price of land, to builders' wages and bricks.

Our analysis shows that the cost of raw materials like timber, steel, plasterboard, concrete and insulation rose in line with general inflation from the 1990s until the Covid-19 pandemic, when they became harder to source.

That was compounded by the impact of the war in Ukraine, which drove up both the cost of energy - 15% in a single year - for making these materials and for use in construction itself. The war in Iran has pushed prices up further.

Even before the pandemic, more than one in five construction firms struggled with a lack of skilled staff, exacerbated by Brexit.

As a guide, a home that cost £150,000 to build in 2015 may cost £230,000 now - analysts say those costs could rise by another 15% in the next five years.

And that's before contending with planning. Strict regulations protect the environment and uphold safety standards but can add costs.

The rising - and increasingly unpredictable - cost of building, coupled with uncertain demand has put some housebuilders off.

As property prices have increased, the deposit needed to buy a house has reached tens of thousands.

The amount to get a 10% deposit varies sharply across the country.

Saving for a deposit becomes particularly hard if you're paying rent too. Private rents typically soak up a third of prospective buyers' incomes.

No surprise a larger number of young people are opting to live at home and pay far lower housing costs so they can save more.

In the past few years house prices have typically risen more slowly than people's wages which, all things being equal, makes it easier for prospective buyers to save.

That has also changed the ratio between house prices and average incomes. Back in 2021, house prices were nearly 9 times average incomes. Today, they're 7.6 times.

And some lenders will take a smaller deposit - sometimes just 5% - which can help overcome the deposit hurdle, a key difficulty of getting on the ladder. People looking to buy can now, in some instances, get a mortgage by saving significantly less money than a few years ago.

If first-time buyers can cobble together a deposit, lenders have recently been more willing to offer larger loans and with longer repayment times. Some buyers can purchase their homes with terms lasting up to 40 years, significantly longer than the usual 25-30 years. That can help lower monthly repayments.

Crucially, too, because property prices are growing more slowly, and interest rates have fallen from their recent peak, mortgage payments relative to wages are moving back towards the long-term average.

Figures from Nationwide show that, if you were a first-time buyer in 2007, your mortgage payments were about 45% of your take-home pay. Today's first-time buyers are paying 32%. That's still above the long-run average of 30%, but it's moving in the right direction.

Smaller deposits and longer mortgage terms are not without risk, however. Those who take that route will end up paying more interest, and are vulnerable to losing money on their property if the value of their homes doesn't increase.

Watch: Millennials have found it hard to buy homes – but there are some changes coming that could help

Ultimately, to make it as easy to get on the ladder as it was for previous generations, we need more homes.

There are moves afoot: Sir Keir Starmer's government introduced plans to streamline planning processes that can be chaotic and slow.

Reforms will also allow more homes to be built on the green belt - not something everyone agrees with.

But to really get things moving, we need to incentivise builders to commit with more confidence to building.

And whatever approach the government takes, the results will take years to come through.

articles.title: US debt has hit $40tn - Will that be a wake-up call?
articles.summary: The US hit a debt milestone this week, but just how worried should we be about the world's largest economy?
articles.body:
What with a 250th birthday, Taylor Swift's wedding and the football World Cup, Americans could be forgiven for taking their eye off the ball this summer.

But signs of economic trouble have been building. This week they hit the headlines when US national debt passed the $40tn (£29.4tn) mark, raising concerns both at home and abroad.

It took almost 200 years for US national debt to reach $1tn for the first time, says Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget.

That milestone back in 1981 was treated as a wake-up call. "At that time, President [Ronald] Reagan told the nation in a televised address, 'If we as a nation needed a warning, let that be it'," she said.

"Jumping to America's 250th year, we are spending more than that just on interest payments on our debt."

Hitting the $40tn milestone was expected - driven by public spending surges under both the Donald Trump and Joe Biden administrations - but it marks another line in the sand.

Ballooning costs for social programmes and other spending have outstripped revenues undermined by tax cuts. Responses to crises such as the 2008 financial crisis and the Covid pandemic have led to increased borrowing.

Add to that higher interest rates in response to recent inflation shocks and the picture begins to look grim.

At the beginning of Trump's first presidential term in 2016, US national debt stood at just under $20tn. It has doubled in the decade since.

The figure is rising by about $90,000 every second, or $7.8bn a day, according to the Congress Joint Economic Committee.

"What's very different now compared to a decade ago is the level of interest rates," says Eric Swanson, professor of economics at University of California and former senior economist at the Federal Reserve.

"Long-term interest rates in the US are at multi-decade highs - part of that is concerns about inflation, but part of that is concerns about the extreme levels of US government borrowing."

The bond market is demanding higher returns with investors wary of the scale of the US's debt, but also because tech firms borrowing eye-watering sums to spend on AI are competing with the government for investors' cash.

"What happens when interest rates go up is that the funding of the deficit becomes more expensive," says economist Mohamed A El-Erian, a professor at the Wharton School.

Interest payments on government debt are now 15% higher than the same period last year, says El-Erian. They are almost 20% of tax revenue, which is "larger than defence", he adds.

The US is nearing its $41.1tn debt ceiling, with debt forecast to climb to about $64tn by 2036, according to the Congressional Budget Office.

But the situation is not yet critical, say economists. The US's position as the world's largest economy and the dollar being the world's reserve currency gives the US a "much longer runway to fiscally misbehave" than other countries, El-Erian says.

"We're getting to a point where it's a flashing yellow light. It's not a flashing red light," he says.

Swanson says other countries have had similar, or higher debt levels.

While US national debt is 126% compared with the size of the economy, it's lower than other G7 nations Japan and Italy.

But investor appetite in lending the US government money through buying bonds is "diminishing", Swanson warns, creating a "vicious" cycle, requiring the government to offer ever higher returns to keep investors purchasing its debt.

And higher US borrowing costs inevitably spill over, raising other countries' borrowing costs too. "What happens in the US never stays in the US," says El-Erian.

Charlie Bean, emeritus economics professor at the London School of Economics, says that if the US debt to economy ratio hits a certain point it could start a fire sale of US bonds and lead to financial market turmoil.

"There probably is a point, but unfortunately we don't know where it is," he says.

"It's not as if there's a fixed number that we could say, you know, 'if it gets to 150 percent, you know, disaster will happen, but we're OK if we stay at 145'."

Households will likely face higher rates for mortgages, car loans and credit cards as a result of the current situation, with those on lower incomes hit hardest, El-Erian says.

There's also a secondary effect on consumers as higher borrowing costs for firms is often passed through to them via higher prices.

So the impact of the debt "finds its way to the pocketbooks of people one way or another," says MacGuineas.

The US's latest figures show the economy slowed in recent months, but it is still growing at a fair lick.

That matters because economic growth means more tax revenue, which can pay for spending, whether that's on government programmes or interest payments. With enough growth, the debt problem is eased, points out El-Erian.

But without sufficient growth the US might have to look at other options. They could include reforming the tax system and public spending, or austerity. Debt restructuring is another option.

The strategy so far employed has been a kind of financial engineering, with the Treasury department on Wednesday stepping in to buy back government debt, boosting demand for bonds and lowering borrowing rates.

But the impact was short-lived with long-term borrowing costs bouncing back up a day later.

With the mid-term elections approaching, the White House will want to be seen to be delivering on the economy. Affordability is the top concern among voters. But the other options are no more appealing and El-Erian is doubtful the government is ready to look at other measures.

"I don't see anything happening that is going to significantly lower the deficit over the next two to three years. If you look at the political talk, it's about tax cuts."

articles.title: In Chinaâs Nizhuhe village, a 945-foot cliffside elevator has cut a dangerous 3-hour school journey to about 30 minutes
articles.summary: China News: For children living in Nizhuhe village in southwest China, getting to school once involved far more than simply setting out for the day. The village l.
articles.body: For children living in Nizhuhe village in southwest China, getting to school once involved far more than simply setting out for the day. The village lies deep within the Nizhu River Grand Canyon, where cliffs and narrow mountain paths separated homes from Guanzhai Village Primary School. A journey that could take around three hours on foot has now been reduced to roughly half an hour, thanks to a transport system built into the canyon itself. Students can travel by shuttle bus, rise hundreds of metres in a cliffside elevator, cross part of the canyon by cable car and then walk the final stretch to school. The latest addition is an even taller elevator, standing 288 metres, or about 945 feet, above the canyon floor. What began as a way to improve access for residents has also helped turn this remote mountain area into an increasingly busy tourist destination. For the pupils, the biggest change is the removal of the most dangerous part of the journey. Instead of navigating steep cliffside paths for hours, they can now make the commute through a series of engineered connections, making regular school attendance safer, faster and far more predictable.Why children in Chinaâs Nizhuhe village once faced a dangerous school journeyNizhuhe village sits deep inside the Nizhu River Grand Canyon, near the border of Yunnan and Guizhou provinces. Guanzhai Village Primary School is positioned much higher up, leaving children at the bottom of the canyon with a difficult route between home and the classroom. Before the new infrastructure was available, the shortest paths were steep, narrow and exposed. Some journeys took more than three hours each way, while reports have also described the round trip as taking close to six hours.The route was not simply a long walk. Children had to negotiate rocky ground, steep sections and paths beside the cliffs. Earlier attempts had been made to make the route safer, including cutting footholds into difficult sections, adding chains and building stone paths and railings. Even with those measures, getting to school remained a demanding part of everyday life. In 2025, Xinhua reported that student Chen Honghan had once considered leaving school because of the difficulty and danger of the journey.Chinaâs Nizhu River Grand Canyon brings elevators and cable cars to the school routeThe first major change came with the development of the Nizhu River Grand Canyon scenic area. A 268-metre sightseeing elevator and an aerial cableway were put into operation in 2022, allowing local villagers to use the facilities free of charge. Instead of climbing the mountainside for hours, pupils could travel by a combination of transport systems that carried them rapidly out of the valley.The trip now involves several short stages rather than one exhausting climb. Children take a scenic shuttle for several minutes, transfer to the elevator and rise vertically by hundreds of metres before continuing by cable car. A final walk completes the route to school. According to the English news, Chen Honghan described the old journey to Xinhua: âBefore, I had to carry my things and walk for three hours on mountain roads to get to school, and if I wasn't careful, I could easily slip and fall.âA second cliffside elevator transforms transport in Chinaâs Nizhu River Grand CanyonThe latest development came in July 2026, when a second cliffside elevator known as Fuyao began operating at the canyon. At 288 metres high, it is roughly 945 feet and stands beside the earlier Qingyun elevator, which rises 268 metres. The two lifts form a dual-elevator system on the canyon wall, expanding transport capacity in an area that has also become a tourist destination.The newer lift is not simply a larger version of the first. China Daily reported that the Fuyao elevator is faster and more spacious, while its shaft extends 20 metres higher than the older installation. The new system is intended to ease pressure as visitor numbers increase, but its effect on residents is also practical. Schoolchildren can continue to use the cliffside route without having to depend on the old mountain paths for their daily journey.How Nizhuhe Grand Canyonâs elevators are transforming tourism and the local economyThe elevators were built as part of a wider effort to develop the Nizhuhe Grand Canyon as a scenic destination. That has given the infrastructure another role. What was once an isolated mountain settlement is now connected to a tourist attraction, with visitors using the elevators and cable cars to move through the canyon. The facilities are also helping residents reach the upper areas without taking the difficult cliff paths.The change has reached into the local economy. In 2024, Xinhua reported that the Nizhuhe Grand Canyon scenic area received about 300,000 visitors and generated nearly 20 million yuan in local revenue. Residents have opened snack shops, guesthouses, farmstays and other small businesses. One villager, Chen Yuqin, told Xinhua that her four-room guesthouse had reached annual gross earnings of as much as 500,000 yuan and that she planned to expand it to 20 rooms.Nizhuhe children see their hometown differently after the canyonâs transformationFor pupils, though, the main difference is much simpler. A route that once required hours of walking is now broken into a sequence of relatively short rides. The children still have to take a shuttle, board an elevator, change to a cable car and walk the final stretch, but the dangerous climb is no longer the central part of getting to class. Xinhua reported that parents in the village also organise a rota, with adults accompanying groups of children on their school journeys.The transformation has given the Nizhuhe children a very different view of the landscape they cross each day. Wang Jiao, a 10-year-old student quoted by Xinhua, said that riding the elevator made her realise how beautiful her hometown was. For the people who built the system, that shift was part of the idea from the beginning. Cai Xiong, chairman of Xuanwei Yatuo Tourism Development Co., Ltd., told Xinhua, âAs a child growing up in the mountains, I never thought it was beautiful.âCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Storms and possible tornadoes pummel the Northeast U.S., flooding roads and damaging beaches
articles.summary: Heavy rain and winds pounded the Northeast U.S. as storms tore through a beach on Long Island, stranded people in their cars in New Jersey and knocked out power in parts of Delaware’s capital city.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Heavy rain and winds pounded the Northeast U.S. on Thursday as storms tore through a beach on Long Island, stranded dozens of people in their cars in New Jersey and knocked out power in parts of Delaware’s capital city. Photos and video shared on social media show debris thrown in the air and pummeling rain as a possible tornado touched down at Atlantic Beach on Long Island’s outer barrier. It tore apart a major beach club, leaving broken beach chairs and wood beams littered across the shoreline. Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman said there were no reports of serious injuries or deaths, but there had been damage to property and a search team was making sure no one was trapped in the cabanas. He declared a state of emergency. “There are reports of people trapped in their vehicles due to flooding in the south shore, and first responders are assisting in their rescue. Photos and video shared on social media show debris thrown in the air and pummeling rain as a possible tornado touched down at Atlantic Beach on Long Island’s outer barrier. It tore apart a major beach club, leaving broken beach chairs and wood beams littered across the shoreline,” he said in a statement. The Sun and Surf Beach Club said buildings had been significantly damaged and it temporarily closed that club and nearby Silver Point. The National Weather Service had warned of waterspouts, tornado-like hazards that happen over water, in the area but wasn’t able to immediately confirm a tornado on the beach. Bryan Ramsey, a meteorologist for the weather service in New York, said the storm was moving East offshore Thursday evening and was expected to taper over the next several hours. In other parts of New York, flooding caused part of the Long Island Expressway in Queens to close in both directions, according to New York City Emergency Management. Photos on social media showed lines of stopped cars as emergency crews traversed the water. In Jersey City, New Jersey, emergency crews rescued 69 people trapped in cars that had been overtaken by flash flooding Thursday, said Mayor James Solomon. Emergency crews waded through roads with knee-high water with small inflatable boats to help those stranded. A likely tornado touched down in Dover, Delaware, and caused significant damage across the city, the police department reported. There were no reports of serious injuries, police said. “Dover — please take this seriously. Stay home. Stay safe,” the department said on Facebook. Photos and video online show fallen trees, downed power lines and flooded roads. The Delaware Electric Cooperative said more than 1,000 customers didn’t have power in the northern part of its service area, but within a few hours most of the outages had been fixed.

articles.title: 'Repeatedly tortured': Imran Khan's sister alleges abuse in jail as ex-Pakistan PM returns to prison
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan's jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she said on Saturday, a day after .
articles.body: Pakistan's jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she said on Saturday, a day after he was taken to a state-run hospital for a brief medical examination and sent back to jail.Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, attended his examination at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad and said the former prime minister was physically fit but had repeatedly complained of torture.âKhan told me that he is being repeatedly tortured in prisonâ, she told the media.The interior and law ministries, along with jail authorities, have not responded to a Reuters request for comment on the allegation.Khan was taken to PIMS overnight on Friday after the Supreme Court had directed authorities to transfer him from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for a medical examination. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours.PTI files contempt petitionKhan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party on Saturday filed a contempt petition against the government, accusing authorities of violating the Supreme Court's order by taking him to PIMS instead of the private hospital named by the court.The petition seeks action against senior government officials and asks that Khan be taken to Shifa International Hospital for treatment, PTI legal adviser Naeem Panjutha said."The petition seeks action against the âprime minister, law minister, information minister" and other government officials, Panjutha said, adding that it also calls for Khan's treatment at the private hospital ordered by the court.The PTI also alleged that Khan was denied access to his personal physician, which it said amounted to another breach of the Supreme Court's directive.A three-judge Supreme Court bench had on Tuesday directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital within two days for a medical examination.The PTI interprets the order as requiring Khan to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September.Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the decision to take Khan to PIMS instead of the court-named private hospital was made because of security concerns.Khan declared medically fit, sent back to jailKhan was examined by a team of doctors, including an ophthalmologist, cardiologist and physician, before being declared medically fit and sent back to Adiala jail in Rawalpindi."A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist and a physician conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit," Tarar said.Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated. The government denies the allegation.His lawyers have previously said his health has deteriorated in prison and that he has suffered substantial loss of vision in his right eye. The government has maintained that medical reports have found no condition requiring immediate treatment.Supporters gather after brief hospital visitKhan's supporters gathered along roads in Islamabad overnight, throwing flowers at a vehicle believed to be carrying him to the hospital.The scenes were broadcast live on Pakistani television, in a notable departure from recent years when broadcasters often avoided mentioning Khan's name.PTI leaders have warned that the latest developments could increase pressure on the government and fuel fresh demonstrations."After what happened yesterday, the pressure (on authorities) will double," Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said, adding that preparations for a protest march planned for September 27 had picked up.Khan's arrest and imprisonment have remained a major source of political tension in Pakistan. His arrest in 2023 triggered widespread protests, including attacks on military installations, and his supporters continue to demand his release.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours.PTI files contempt petitionKhan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party on Saturday filed a contempt petition against the government, accusing authorities of violating the Supreme Court's order by taking him to PIMS instead of the private hospital named by the court.The petition seeks action against senior government officials and asks that Khan be taken to Shifa International Hospital for treatment, PTI legal adviser Naeem Panjutha said."The petition seeks action against the âprime minister, law minister, information minister" and other government officials, Panjutha said, adding that it also calls for Khan's treatment at the private hospital ordered by the court.The PTI also alleged that Khan was denied access to his personal physician, which it said amounted to another breach of the Supreme Court's directive.A three-judge Supreme Court bench had on Tuesday directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital within two days for a medical examination.The PTI interprets the order as requiring Khan to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September.Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the decision to take Khan to PIMS instead of the court-named private hospital was made because of security concerns.Khan declared medically fit, sent back to jailKhan was examined by a team of doctors, including an ophthalmologist, cardiologist and physician, before being declared medically fit and sent back to Adiala jail in Rawalpindi."A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist and a physician conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit," Tarar said.Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated. The government denies the allegation.His lawyers have previously said his health has deteriorated in prison and that he has suffered substantial loss of vision in his right eye. The government has maintained that medical reports have found no condition requiring immediate treatment.Supporters gather after brief hospital visitKhan's supporters gathered along roads in Islamabad overnight, throwing flowers at a vehicle believed to be carrying him to the hospital.The scenes were broadcast live on Pakistani television, in a notable departure from recent years when broadcasters often avoided mentioning Khan's name.PTI leaders have warned that the latest developments could increase pressure on the government and fuel fresh demonstrations."After what happened yesterday, the pressure (on authorities) will double," Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said, adding that preparations for a protest march planned for September 27 had picked up.Khan's arrest and imprisonment have remained a major source of political tension in Pakistan. His arrest in 2023 triggered widespread protests, including attacks on military installations, and his supporters continue to demand his release.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Iran discovers over 7.5 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves as US blockade squeezes energy sector
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iran has discovered more than 7.5 trillion cubic feet (tcf) of natural gas in its southern Fars province, even as months of conflict with the US and I.
articles.body: Iran has discovered more than 7.5 trillion cubic feet (tcf) of natural gas in its southern Fars province, even as months of conflict with the US and Israel have disrupted the country's energy sector.Around 5.7 tcf of the newly discovered gas is recoverable, Iranian oil minister Mohsen Paknejad told state television on Sunday. He said the recoverable reserves were equivalent to around 15 years of production from one phase of South Pars, the world's largest gas field, which Iran shares with Qatar.The discovery also includes gas condensates worth âtens of billions of dollarsâ, Paknejad said, adding that Iran plans to develop the resources âas soon as possible.âHowever, actual production is likely to take years. Iran's energy sector was already struggling with Western sanctions, underinvestment and power shortages before the latest conflict.War hits Iran's gas productionIran lost around a quarter of its daily gas production capacity after attacks on energy infrastructure began in late February, according to Bloomberg. The attacks included strikes on facilities at South Pars.Although some production capacity has since returned, the Iranian government has warned of possible gas shortages this winter and urged citizens to reduce consumption.The latest discovery comes as Tehran faces growing economic and energy pressures amid its confrontation with Washington.Hormuz tensions escalateTensions between the US and Iran also intensified over the Strait of Hormuz, a key global energy corridor. US President Donald Trump again shared an image on Truth Social depicting the strategically important waterway as ânew US territoryâ, after sharing the same graphic on August 18. Trump had earlier said, âPretty soon I'll be declaring the Strait of Hormuz a territory of the United Statesâ.Iran has rejected the US territorial claims and maintained that the waterway will remain closed unless Washington changes its position.Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei criticised Trump's remarks, saying, âThe gap between America's inability to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and its claim to own it is greater than the 7,000-mile distance between Washington and the Strait itself,â adding, âWelcome to the post-American order in the Persian Gulf.âThe confrontation comes as the US prepares additional economic measures against Tehran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce what he has described as âthe toughest sanctions in historyâ against Iran and has urged China to cooperate with Washington over Iranian oil shipments.Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei criticised the planned measures, saying, âSuch secondary sanctions find no foundation in international law,â in a post on X on August 22.Rezaei also warned neighbouring countries against supporting the US measures. âWe are telling all nearby countries not to join the US economic war, otherwise we will consider them as enemies,â he said.Despite the escalating rhetoric, Iranian officials have indicated that Tehran remains open to diplomacy. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for diplomatic engagement to resolve the standoff, while stressing that Iran must protect its national strength and dignity.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Burnham to hand long-range missile blueprints as he visits Kyiv
articles.summary: It comes after Moscow warned of "consequences" over the reported use of British drones by Ukraine.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has promised to keep up the pressure on Russia despite Moscow's "outrageous threats", on his first official visit to Ukraine as UK prime minister.

Burnham met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and chaired his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

He said the coalition was "doing everything we can" while urging the US Congress to "ratchet up" economic pressure on Russia.

The government has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile - allowing Ukraine to produce the long-range weapon domestically.

UK missiles offer may help Ukraine - but they are not what Zelensky needs most Published 1 day ago

UK missiles offer may help Ukraine - but they are not what Zelensky needs most

Briton fighting for Russia killed in Ukraine Published 1 day ago

Briton fighting for Russia killed in Ukraine

Burnham said allies were doing "everything we can" to "dig into our own stocks and help others dig into their stocks" of air defences to protect Ukraine.

"This is the moment to keep up the pressure on Russia, the moment to squeeze their ability to fund this illegal war," Burnham said, praising the "strength" of the Ukrainian people.

"Ukraine has been Europe's protector, not a drain on our security but the front line in keeping Europe safe."

It comes after Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov criticised the UK's decision to share the missile blueprints. Peskov said it prevented "even the slightest progress" towards achieving peace.

He told reporters on Monday that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate any missile production sites to destroy them.

"Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire," he added.

In response, Burnham said: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?"

He said the issue of missile interceptors would be the main topic at the coalition of the willing meeting.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, former Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrei Fedorov said the UK could face a "semi-military" response in retaliation for sharing military blueprints with Ukraine, but specified this would be "not by Russia, but from unknown sources".

"Something might happen with enterprises, with factories which are producing drones for Ukraine," Fedorov said.

Asked if he was OK with a potential attack, he said: "No, I don't think it's okay, because the problem is that we are now facing, in front of the danger, that Ukrainian conflict will be beyond Ukrainian borders."

Burnham has been reaffirming the UK's backing for Kyiv in the wake of escalating Russian strikes on Ukraine in recent weeks - including one on a shopping centre on Friday that killed at least 16 people.

In a joint statement after the meeting, Burnham and co-chairs French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the group would aim to strength Kyiv's air defences "as a matter or urgent priority".

They also condemned Moscow's "systemic and escalating strikes against Ukraine's cities, critical infrastructure and civilians" and pledged to "constrain Russia's war chest through sanctions and actions against the "shadow fleet".

The Coalition of the Willing is a partnership of 34 countries including Ukraine. Members met on Monday in either Kyiv or by video conference, with a release stating "leaders once again reaffirmed their commitment to support Ukraine's independence".

It came as the European Union said it had released â¬6.1bn (Â£5.2bn) in military aid for Ukraine to boost its air defences. The finance is part of a wider â¬90bn loan from the EU to Ukraine.

The UK and Ukraine have also announced a new military technology partnership , external giving British experts access to Kyiv's Avengers AI Labs database.

Downing Street says Ukraine has used sensors and cameras to capture data across the battlefield and it can be used to train AI models "to solve key national security challenges" faced by both countries.

On Monday morning the prime minister laid flowers at the graves of Ukrainian soldiers during a service at the National Military Memorial Cemetery.

He accepted an award from Zelensky on behalf of the British people recognising the UK's support for Ukraine during an independence day event outside the St Sofia cathedral in Kyiv.

In a speech, Burnham compared Ukraine's resistance to Russia to the UK's fight with Nazi Germany, saying: "My nation kept the flame of European freedom alive in the 20th century, you hold that flame in the 21st."

In a statement issued ahead of the visit, the prime minister said: "On Ukraine's 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.

"I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine's security is our security."

He said the friendship Ukraine shared with the UK would "long outlast Russia's illegal war", adding: "Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace."

Moscow earlier warned of "consequences" over the use of British drones by Ukraine in its recent ramping up of strikes on Russian infrastructure.

Kyiv has stepped up long-range attacks on Moscow and other Russian regions, targeting oil refineries and warehouses of the country's largest online retailer, Wildberries.

The government is allowing UK defence company MBDA to declassify information on its components for the Scalp missile, as Ukraine and France aim to establish assembly lines in Ukraine.

Scalp missiles and its UK-produced version, the Storm Shadow, have already been provided to Kyiv by both Britain and France and used to hit military targets inside Russia.

What are the Storm Shadow missiles Ukraine has fired into Russia?

Ukraine hopes it can also be given more Patriot interceptor missiles, with Zelensky again asking for more of the weapon, which are used to combat Russia's ballistic missiles.

Ukraine has been relying on American supplies of the Patriots, but its stockpiles are running low due to the war in Iran, leaving Ukraine vulnerable to Russian attacks.

The Russian embassy in the UK has accused Britain of "deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis", saying "the deeper its involvement in the conflict... the higher the price it will pay".

In response, Burnham said last week: "We are not fair-weather friends, we will be there in Ukraine's hour of need and that won't change."

Asked on Tuesday about the Russian threat, Burnham maintained the UK was "providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself and that's been the British position all the way through this conflict, by previous prime ministers - it remains the case with me".

The visit comes as Russia confirmed its ambassador to the UK, Andrei Kelin, had left his post in London in recent weeks.

The Kremlin is yet to put forward a replacement but Russia's embassy to the UK told the BBC it did not reflect an intention to downgrade diplomatic relations between the two nations.

Deadly exchanges between Russia and Ukraine continued overnight, with two children killed and seven injured when Ukrainian drone debris hit a private children's centre in Russia, local authorities say.

A warehouse belonging to online retailer Ozon was also set on fire, two days after Ukraine said it would target the company for selling dual use items that could be used by the military.

It was at the third night in the row that Ozon's warehouses had been targeted, with the company confirming on Saturday that a logistics centre in the Samara region had been hit and a warehouse in Orenburg on Sunday.

Three people were also killed in a Russian attack on the north-eastern Ukrainian city of Kharkiv, regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said.

articles.title: 'Did not meet launch conditions': China's unmanned moon mission delayed last minute
articles.summary: China News: China has postponed the planned launch of its Chang'e-7 Moon mission, days after saying the launch site and equipment were in good condition.The probe.
articles.body: China has postponed the planned launch of its Chang'e-7 Moon mission, days after saying the launch site and equipment were in good condition.The probe and the Long March 5 rocket assigned to carry it had already been transferred to the takeoff area at the Wenchang Space Launch Center in southern Hainan province last week. As of Wednesday, inspections were still due to be carried out and the agency said the launch was "scheduled for the coming period".On Sunday, China's manned space agency said a "comprehensive assessment" had found that the mission "does not meet launch conditions and cannot take place during the planned window this year". It did not identify which conditions had not been met or say when the mission could be rescheduled. Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported the announcement.Chang'e-7 is designed to search for water at the Moon's south pole. Media reports had indicated that it could lift off either over the weekend or on Monday.The agency said the postponement was "based on the principle of prudence, reliability and absolute mission success". It provided no further details behind the decision.The delay also comes just under two weeks after a rare launch failure from Wenchang. Media reports showed a rocket launched from the Hainan site exploding as crowds watched a fiery ball in the sky.State news agency Xinhua said the failed mission used a Long March 7A carrier rocket that had taken off from the Wenchang Space Launch Site. The rocket was carrying the Zhongxing-4B communications satellite when an "anomaly" occurred during flight.Xinhua said the cause of the failure remained under investigation.The two developments come as Beijing continues to expand its space programme, into which it has invested billions of dollars in recent years. President Xi Jinping has described the country's ambitions in space as its "space dream".China also successfully landed a reusable rocket for the first time in July, according to its space agency. The milestone represented an advance in China's space programme, including its efforts to reduce launch costs.Chang'e-7 forms part of China's wider push to put astronauts on the Moon before 2030. The United States is competing in the same race through its Artemis programme.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Norway's King Harald V's health has worsened, palace says
articles.summary: Norway's King Harald remains in hospital receiving antibiotics for a bloodstream bacterial infection.
articles.body:
King Harald V of Norway's health has worsened, the palace has said, as he remains in hospital receiving antibiotics for a bacterial infection in his bloodstream.

The monarch has responded to treatment despite the deterioration in his condition, according to the palace, but he will remain at Oslo University Hospital, Rikshospitalet, and on leave from royal duties until further notice.

The 89-year-old, who has been on the throne since 1991, was admitted to hospital and put on sick leave a week ago.

His son, Crown Prince Haakon, 53, has been serving as regent while his father is on leave.

King Harald has been treated in recent weeks with cortisone for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia. It causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced, and leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.

In April 2024, Norway's royal household said that King Harald would make a "permanent reduction" to his public engagements "out of consideration for his age". That year, the king had been fitted with a pacemaker after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia.

The Norwegian royal family has already faced a challenging year in 2026.

Crown Prince Haakon's wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit, received a lung transplant in June after she had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018.

The transplant came two days after Mette-Marit's son Marius Borg HÃ¸iby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. He had denied the most serious charges and his lawyers said he would appeal the sentence.

HÃ¸iby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure.

Also earlier in the year, documents were released revealing Mette-Marit's frequent contact with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

She later apologised to Norway's king and queen for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement", adding in a national TV interview that she wished she had never met him.

In April 2024, Norway's royal household said that King Harald would make a "permanent reduction" to his public engagements "out of consideration for his age". That year, the king had been fitted with a pacemaker after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia.
The Norwegian royal family has already faced a challenging year in 2026.
Crown Prince Haakon's wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit, received a lung transplant in June after she had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018.

The transplant came two days after Mette-Marit's son Marius Borg HÃ¸iby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. He had denied the most serious charges and his lawyers said he would appeal the sentence.
HÃ¸iby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure.
Also earlier in the year, documents were released revealing Mette-Marit's frequent contact with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
She later apologised to Norway's king and queen for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement", adding in a national TV interview that she wished she had never met him.

articles.title: ‘Not everything was perfect': Bryson DeChambeau's curious LIV comments raise questions
articles.summary: Following LIV Golf's season finale, Bryson DeChambeau offered up some conflicting thoughts on the league's future that raised questions.
articles.body:
The dust is still settling from LIV Golf's 2026 season finale in Indianapolis . The question now is whether it will prove to be the final LIV Golf tournament in history. Bryson DeChambeau didn't provide much clarity on the matter Sunday night.

Instead, DeChambeau offered up conflicting thoughts on LIV's future, at first professing his excitement at "what could happen next year," before talking about LIV in the past tense and even acknowledging unspecified mistakes the upstart league has made.

DeChambeau after LIV's season finale: 'We did something different in the game'

After a year of increasingly bad news, LIV's season came to an abrupt end on Sunday night at LIV Golf Indianapolis.

With the season-ending Team Championship cancelled, both the season-long individual winner (Jon Rahm) and the 2026 team winner (Rahm's Legion XIII) were determined.

DeChambeau finished T3 in Indy , leaving him in second place in the final Individual standings, while his Crushers team failed to make the final podium.

With funding for the league gone, thanks to the PIF's decision to cut its losses earlier this year , no one knows if a 2027 LIV season will happen.

'We have a lot against us': Bryson DeChambeau gets real about LIV's uncertain future

While Phil Mickelson was the primary force behind the creation of LIV Golf, DeChambeau was always the league's biggest star and public booster. With the league's future in doubt, that remains the case… to a point.

Even after Sunday's round was over, DeChambeau was still expressing optimism for what the future holds for LIV, at least at first.

"I think there's a lot of potential moving forward. It's been an interesting ride, that's for sure," DeChambeau said Sunday night. "You know just as much as I have everything that we've gone through and the tough moments that we've had. But it's made us stronger."

He then invoked the concept of LIV 2.0, which the league's CEO hopes will be anchored by new big-money investors , and revealed he has "great thoughts" about next season without divulging any details.

"As much as we're transitioning from LIV 1.0 to 2.0, I have great thoughts about what could happen next year. I wish I could be more up front about it," DeChambeau said.

However, after his initial positivity, DeChambeau then switched to talking about LIV Golf in the past tense and alluded to mistakes the league made over the years.

"But ultimately I'm proud of the fact of what we've done, the good and some of the bad that we've unfortunately had, things that have occurred," DeChambeau said. "I'm going to be real with it; not everything was perfect. But for the most part we've done a solid job."

But his closing line should raise the most questions among observers and fans interested in what the future holds for LIV, if there is a future at all. Bryson again delivered it in the past tense.

"If there's one thing that I could say, it's we did something different in the game of golf, and I'm proud of that."

That sounds an awful lot like LIV's biggest proponent is resigned to the fact that the league might be finished for good.

articles.title: From Gen Z wave to heat in 150 days: Balen faces street anger, parl pressure and party unease
articles.summary: South Asia News: Barely 150 days after Gen Z anger helped propel Balendra âBalenâ Shah to Nepalâs top job, the same restless street energy that propelled his rise seem.
articles.body: Barely 150 days after Gen Z anger helped propel Balendra âBalenâ Shah to Nepalâs top job, the same restless street energy that propelled his rise seems to be pinning him down, leaving the former rapper and Kathmandu mayor under pressure from public protests, Parliament and his own Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP).Barely two months after he took office, young protesters returned to Kathmanduâs Maitighar Mandala demanding his resignation, while opposition MPs attacked his repeated absence from Parliament, where he attended only five of the first 39 sittings before Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal directed him to appear and answer lawmakers on Aug 26.The political honeymoon began fraying within weeks of Shah taking office on March 27 after RSP swept 182 of 275 House seats. In April, strict enforcement of customs rules on goods brought across the open India border hit people dependent on Indian markets for groceries, medicines and household essentials, triggering protests in border towns and forcing authorities to relax the move.Public anger intensified in July after 25-year-old ride-share driver Ganesh Nepali self-immolated outside the passport office in Kathmandu following a dispute over municipal action against his vehicle. His death fuelled demonstrations over municipal policing and revived criticism of drives against informal settlements and landless squatters without adequate rehabilitation.Shah also faced sustained attacks over Nepalâs border dispute with India after telling Parliament, âAfter becoming PM, I came to know that not only has India encroached on Nepalâs land, but Nepal has also encroached on Indiaâs land.â Opposition parties demanded evidence, withdrawal of the statement and an apology.Pressure also came from Nepalâs media fraternity. Federation of Nepali Journalists (FNJ) alleged in May that senior journalist Kishore Shrestha faced police surveillance, an attempted arrest and threats after his publication carried reports critical of a minister and ruling-party leaders.Violent communal clashes in southern Nepal along the border with India added another layer of pressure and forced Shah to address the nation after criticism over his delayed response, while in Pokhara former Gorkha servicemen, their families and prospective recruits continued demanding a resolution of stalled recruitment of Nepalis into Indian Army under Agnipath.The strain meanwhile has spread inside RSP, where lawmakers and senior leaders questioned Shahâs distance from party structures and unilateral governing style, with party insiders saying he had shown âlittle faith in the party system itselfâ. RSP MP Jagadish Kharel sharpened the criticism from within while speaking in Parliament, saying, âThis govt will not survive if only the dignity of the Prime Minister is preserved. Our dignity must also be preservedâ. The unease was serious enough for home minister Sudan Gurung to urge colleagues at RSPâs Aug 19 parliamentary-party discussion to "contain" their differences rather than carry them into House. âLetâs keep the quarrels at home, letâs not oppose (the govt) in the House; the opposition is beginning to grow stronger,â he said.
