articles.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner jailed after prostitution arrest
articles.summary: Jed York pleaded no contest to two charges in Ohio after being arrested for soliciting prostitution.
articles.body:
Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York has been jailed in Ohio after being arrested for soliciting prostitution.

The 45-year-old, who is also the owner of the San Francisco 49ers, was convicted of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after pleading no contest to two charges.

In the Ohio legal system, a no contest plea means a defendant accepts a conviction without formally admitting guilt.

York was sentenced to one day in jail on each offence, to be served concurrently, and was given credit for time already served.

York was fined $150 for disorderly conduct and $1,000 for possessing criminal tools.

Court records show the case was brought by East Palestine Police Department and filed at Columbiana County Municipal Court on Monday.

York pleaded no contest to both charges at an arraignment hearing and was found guilty.

Court records also show an expungement request was filed and denied on the same day. This is a request to have records destroyed or sealed so they are not accessible to the public.

According to reports in the US media, other court documents say York responded to an advertisement on a prostitution website placed by undercover officers from a Human Trafficking Task Force in Ohio.

These documents say he arranged to have sexual activity with a woman in exchange for $140 (Â£103).

In a plea deal, the original charge was reduced to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools - thought to refer to the phone used to reply to the advert.

The 49ers were part of the US consortium who took control of Rangers last year but York is not involved in the day-to-day running of the club.

Rangers and Leeds have both said they will not be commenting.

The 49ers said: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."

York became a co-owner of Rangers through 49ers Enterprises, the investment arm linked to the NFL's San Francisco 49ers, where he serves as chief executive and principal owner.

In May 2025, a consortium led by US businessman Andrew Cavenagh and 49ers Enterprises completed a takeover of Rangers after acquiring a controlling 51% stake in the Scottish Premiership club.

Cavenagh became Rangers chairman, with 49ers Enterprises taking a leading role in the club's ownership.

The takeover followed months of negotiations and brought Rangers under majority American-backed ownership.

49ers Enterprises first invested in Leeds United in 2018 when the club was in the Championship, steadily increasing its investment as the Whites returned to the Premier League following a 16-year absence, before assuming full control in 2023.

As an NFL owner, York is subject to league policies. "We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy," the NFL said.

articles.title: US diplomats heading back to Middle East as immediate Iran war risk recedes: Report
articles.summary: US News: The United States is preparing to return diplomats to several Middle Eastern embassies that were evacuated during the war with Iran, according to a re.
articles.body: The United States is preparing to return diplomats to several Middle Eastern embassies that were evacuated during the war with Iran, according to a report by the New York Times. The move suggests Washington does not expect a return to full-scale fighting in the immediate future.According to an internal State Department document cited by NYT, Foreign Service officers could begin returning to their posts as early as this week. The plan covers US diplomatic missions in Israel, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Oman, Iraq and Kuwait.The US Embassy in Lebanon is expected to be the first to receive returning diplomats, although it will continue operating below full staffing. Under the plan, staffing would eventually return to full strength in Israel, Jordan and Oman.Embassies in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Lebanon would initially operate at up to 85% staffing, while missions in Iraq, Kuwait and Bahrain would be capped at 75%.The State Department said it was continually reviewing security conditions at its diplomatic missions and adjusting staffing levels to allow the US to pursue its foreign-policy objectives while protecting personnel.The planned return comes despite the fact that US-Iran talks have stalled and Washington has continued to increase economic pressure on Tehran.The US announced a fresh round of sanctions on August 24 targeting Iranian military activities, procurement networks, cyber operations and petroleum trade.The decision to bring diplomats back nevertheless represents a significant shift from earlier this year. The US began reducing its diplomatic presence in the region after tensions with Iran escalated in February, with nonessential personnel and family members evacuated from several posts. Some embassies were subsequently hit or targeted by drones and rockets during the conflict.Former US officials said the redeployment could indicate that Washington believes the immediate risk of renewed fighting has fallen. But they cautioned that it should not be interpreted as proof of a lasting peace. Restrictions on family members at several Gulf missions also suggest that the State Department continues to see an elevated security threat.The move is less a declaration that the Iran conflict is over and more a signal that Washington believes its diplomats can begin returning while the fragile post-war standoff continues.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Kate Hudson to produce How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days sequel, 23 years on
articles.summary: Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, her co-star from the 2003 rom-com, could be reunited for the sequel.
articles.body:
A sequel to How to Lose a Guy In 10 Days is in development, more than 20 years after the original hit rom-com was released, with original star Kate Hudson set to produce.

Work on the film is in the "very early days", with sources telling US media that both Hudson, 47, and Matthew McConaughey, 56, could reprise their roles from the first film.

In the original, Hudson played a magazine journalist called Andie who researches an article about modern dating. She convinces her boss she can get a man, Benjamin (McConaughey), to leave her in 10 days. Meanwhile, Benjamin bets his boss he can make any woman fall for him, with Andie his target.

Hudson will produce the sequel alongside Stacey Sher, who is behind hits such as Pulp Fiction and Matilda.

The movie grossed nearly $180m worldwide at the box office at the time.

The yellow silk Carolina Herrera dress Hudson wore near the end of the film also became a much talked-about piece of modern cinema fashion.

The star's most recent film role was in 2025's Song Sung Blue, which earned her a second Oscar nomination, following her first nod for Almost Famous back in 2001.

McConaughey's films include Dallas Buyer's Club, which won him an Oscar in 2014, The Wedding Planner and Magic Mike. He also appeared in 2008 movie Fool's Gold alongside Hudson.

Representatives for Hudson and McConaughey have been contacted for comment.

The new film would be the latest in a trend for nostalgic sequels in Hollywood, following The Devil Wears Prada 2 - which came 20 years after the original and also featured a magazine employee called Andy (played by Anne Hathaway).

In 2024, McConaughey told People magazine about his first meeting with Hudson before filming How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days.

"Immediately, we were comfortable with each other, and we jacked with each other, and we busted each other's chops, and we laughed a lot," he recalled.

"There was a bit of rock and roll exchange, like, 'Oh, this could be some heavyweight fun.' And I think that's why I was cast, and that's why, for whatever extent, it worked."

articles.title: âWe are under attackâ: US military aircraft lands in Russia, sparks wild theories
articles.summary: US News: A US Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster III military transport aircraft landed at Moscowâs Vnukovo Airport on Tuesday, news agency AFP reported citing .
articles.body: A US Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster III military transport aircraft landed at Moscowâs Vnukovo Airport on Tuesday, news agency AFP reported citing flight tracking data. This triggered speculation over the unexplained purpose of the highly unusual flight at a time when US-Russia contacts over the Ukraine war have lost momentum.The aircraft, operating as RCH4555, flew from Riga, Latvia, to Moscow, according to publicly available Flightradar24 data. It departed Riga at around 8:50am Moscow time and landed at Vnukovo shortly after 10am. Footage of the aircraftâs arrival showed a cameraman apparently joking, âwe are under attack!â as the US military plane descended towards the airport.The flight immediately attracted attention because the aircraftâs previous movements showed that it had arrived in Riga on August 23 from Camp Springs, Maryland, where Joint Base Andrews is located. The base is closely associated with US presidential air transport, including Air Force One. However, the presence of a C-17 does not by itself indicate that a senior US official was aboard.From Andrews to Moscow: What we know about the mystery flightThe Kremlin said it had no information about the aircraftâs arrival. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov also said there were no meetings with US administration officials planned in Moscow this week, according to comments cited by Newsweek.The US European Command likewise had no information to offer when approached about the flight-tracking data, Newsweek reported. No official explanation has been given for the aircraftâs passengers, cargo or mission.That lack of information has fuelled theories that the flight could be linked to diplomatic contacts between Washington and Moscow. The timing is particularly notable as efforts to advance negotiations over the Ukraine war have slowed. Reports have suggested that Moscow remains open to new US proposals, while Ukraine, Washington and European officials have been working on a fresh proposal for Russia.Some military aviation observers have also speculated about a possible connection to US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. However, Pentagon records reportedly placed Hegseth in Nebraska and Wisconsin on Monday as part of his âArsenal of Freedomâ tour, making it unclear whether the aircraft had any connection to his movements.What makes the C-17 Globemaster III significantThe C-17 Globemaster III is a heavy strategic transport aircraft designed to rapidly move troops, vehicles and large cargo over long distances. According to US Air Force specifications, it can carry a maximum payload of about 170,900 pounds, or 77,500kg.Its large cargo hold can accommodate military vehicles and other oversized equipment, while the aircraft can also conduct tactical airlift, airdrop operations and aeromedical evacuation missions. It is capable of operating from relatively short and austere runways, adding to its flexibility.The aircraft measures about 53 metres in length and has a wingspan of nearly 52 metres. It is powered by four Pratt & Whitney F117 turbofan engines and can fly at a cruising speed of around 450 knots.The C-17's design means it can serve a range of missions, from moving military equipment between bases to supporting government or diplomatic operations. That versatility is one reason its unexplained appearance in Moscow has generated so much speculation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

No official explanation has been given for the aircraftâs passengers, cargo or mission.That lack of information has fuelled theories that the flight could be linked to diplomatic contacts between Washington and Moscow. The timing is particularly notable as efforts to advance negotiations over the Ukraine war have slowed. Reports have suggested that Moscow remains open to new US proposals, while Ukraine, Washington and European officials have been working on a fresh proposal for Russia.Some military aviation observers have also speculated about a possible connection to US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. However, Pentagon records reportedly placed Hegseth in Nebraska and Wisconsin on Monday as part of his âArsenal of Freedomâ tour, making it unclear whether the aircraft had any connection to his movements.What makes the C-17 Globemaster III significantThe C-17 Globemaster III is a heavy strategic transport aircraft designed to rapidly move troops, vehicles and large cargo over long distances. According to US Air Force specifications, it can carry a maximum payload of about 170,900 pounds, or 77,500kg.Its large cargo hold can accommodate military vehicles and other oversized equipment, while the aircraft can also conduct tactical airlift, airdrop operations and aeromedical evacuation missions. It is capable of operating from relatively short and austere runways, adding to its flexibility.The aircraft measures about 53 metres in length and has a wingspan of nearly 52 metres. It is powered by four Pratt & Whitney F117 turbofan engines and can fly at a cruising speed of around 450 knots.The C-17's design means it can serve a range of missions, from moving military equipment between bases to supporting government or diplomatic operations. That versatility is one reason its unexplained appearance in Moscow has generated so much speculation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: LASK to hold silence for Celtic fan who died during Champions League match
articles.summary: The 65-year-old supporter took ill during the first leg of the Champions League play-off in Glasgow last week.
articles.body:
Austrian champions LASK have held a silence in memory of a Celtic supporter who died when the sides met in Glasgow last week.

The 65-year-old fan became ill in the stadium during the first leg of the Champions League play-off at Celtic Park on Wednesday.

He was taken to Glasgow Royal Infirmary but died a short time later.

Ahead of the return leg in Linz - which kicked off at 20:00 - LASK confirmed they wished to pay tribute to the supporter.

O'Neill predicts 'tough old night' as Celtic take 3-0 lead to LASK

Duran scores twice as Celtic beat LASK to take big step towards Champions League

During the silence, fans held a banner that read: "Rest in peace, James".

Writing on social media, Celtic said: "LASK has contacted Celtic to advise that they wish to observe a period of silence prior to tonight's match in tribute to our supporter who fell ill and tragically passed away following last week's first leg at Celtic Park.

"We send our thanks and appreciation to LASK."

Last week Celtic thanked the emergency services and fellow fans for their efforts in dealing with the "tragic incident".

A club statement added: "We extend our deepest condolences, thoughts and prayers to the family and we will ensure that we offer them our full support at this extremely difficult time."

Martin O'Neill's team hold a 3-0 advantage going into the match at the Raiffeisen Arena.

The winner will progress to the lucrative group stage of the Champions League.

articles.title: Canada announces 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs on US as high as 50%
articles.summary: The latest escalation in an ongoing trade war between the US and Canada will see new levies on goods from steel to furniture, fresh tuna and makeup.
articles.body:
Canada has announced counter-tariffs as high as 50% on a range of US goods in retaliation to the latest wave of levies on Canadian imports imposed by President Donald Trump last weekend.

The Canadian tariffs will apply to nearly C$28bn ($20bn; £15bn) worth of American products, ranging from steel to furniture, fresh tuna and cotton T-shirts, officials announced on Tuesday.

The list of targeted products is designed to match Canadian goods hit by the US. The Canadian levies are set to come into effect on 8 September.

It is the latest escalation after US-Canada trade talks collapsed late last week, with each side accusing the other of making last-minute demands that were unreasonable.

Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said that Canada's retaliation is in response to 50% tariffs imposed by the Trump administration on a range of Canadian goods after trade talks fell apart on Friday.

"Those tariffs will have real consequences for Canadian workers, businesses and communities across our nation," he said. "Canada must respond."

Champagne characterised Canada's retaliation as "proportionate" and "strategic".

He added that Canada will also offer businesses and workers impacted by US tariffs an additional C$7.5bn for support programmes designed to minimise job losses and keep companies afloat.

Placing taxes on trade between what are historically two of the world's closest trading partners will undoubtedly lead to pain on both sides of the border.

Supply chains which have been developed over decades are set to see increased trading costs due the latest tariff announcements made from both the US and Canada, ultimately hitting businesses of all sizes and consumers through potentially higher prices.

Polls suggest the majority of Canadians support their government in holding firm against the US.

But some questions remain on exactly why trade talks fell apart, with the Conservative opposition asking that the full text of the draft deal with the US be released.

Businesses have also expressed concerns about the impact of a prolonged trade war with Canada's largest trading partner.

The White House released a statement after Canada announced its counter-tariffs, saying that the US was prepared to offer Canada "the most preferential market access of any country on Earth" in recent trade talks.

"Instead of partnership, Canada chose unreasonable demands, walk-backs, and flat-out rejection," it said.

In a series of Tuesday posts on Truth Social, Trump also accused Canada of "ripping off" the US for decades and of charging American farmers steep tariffs.

"I deal with many countries, and Canada is easily the most difficult and unreasonable," Trump wrote. "They feel entitled, but they are not a State, and will be entitled no longer!"

He suggested that he will change the name of Lake Ontario, one of the Great Lakes on the US-Canada border, to Lake America, writing: "We don't expect to doing much business with Ontario any longer."

Trump threatened this week to hike US tariffs on Canadian automobiles to 50% as of 1 January.

Prime Minister Mark Carney responded by accusing Trump of wanting to "destroy" Canadian industries including the automobile manufacturing and steel and aluminum sectors.

Public rhetoric on both sides reached a fever pitch on Monday, but some officials struck a more diplomatic tone on Tuesday with hopes that talks could be resumed.

After calling Trump a "loser" on Monday at a news conference, Ontario Premier Doug Ford acknowledged in an interview with CNN that "things got a little heated".

"But I want to make a deal — a good deal for the American people, a good deal for Canadians," Ford said.

The escalation also puts into question the future of a North American free trade pact between Canada, the US and Mexico called the USMCA.

President Claudia Sheinbaum had despatched her economy secretary, Marcelo Ebrard, to Washington for emergency talks after trade negotiations collapsed with Canada.

How Canada could hit back to hurt the US economy - and Trump

'Half my business will be gone' - firms in Canada and US fear trade war

Canada released on Tuesday a list of nearly 900 US products that will be hit by its counter-tariffs.

A 50% tariff on steel and aluminum products that were previously only subject to a 25% counter tariff

A 50% tariff on various other goods including natural honey, furniture, clothing and apparel, makeup and perfume

A 25% tariff on goods including appliances, like dishwashers and washing machines, dairy products, such as cheese, fish and seafood, and certain steel and aluminum derivative products

A 15% tariff on certain types of tools and machinery, including forklifts and air conditioning machines

Canadian officials said they chose products that consumers and businesses in Canada could source elsewhere in an attempt to minimise hurt at home.

articles.title: Foreign students must make an official request for authorization: ICE issues new memo as colleges pause CPT program; American students will also have to complete training
articles.summary: US News: As US universities started pausing CPT (Curricular Practical Training), which is a temporary work authorization for F-1 students, triggering confusion.
articles.body: As US universities started pausing CPT (Curricular Practical Training), which is a temporary work authorization for F-1 students, triggering confusion over the future of international students in the US, Immigration and Customs Enforcement issued another memo clarifying and doubling down on the new restrictions. CPT allows F-1 students to gain off-campus work experience, internships, before graduating and hence it has to be related to the student's major. For approval of these internships, students do not have to go to immigration; the university itself can approve them. ICE said the university administration is not giving these approvals judiciously.On August 12, ICE issued a directive to all schools and universities stating that CPT has to be an integral part of the course. Many universities, including UC Berkeley, UC Davis, UC San Diego, Purdue, Santa Clara paused the approvals of CPT programs.In the new memo, ICE explained some of the frequently asked questions and made it clear that all students attending the same course must do CPT as it must be mandatory. American students, too, will have to do this, otherwise it's not valid because it's not mandatory then.How is CPT defined in regulation?A foreign student may be authorized by a DSO (Designated School Official) to participate in a CPT program that is an integral part of an established curriculum. Curricular practical training is defined as alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education or any other type of required internship or practicum that is offered by sponsoring employers through cooperative agreements with the school.How is CPT different from Optional Practical Training?Optional Practical Training (OPT) is training that is not an integral part of a studentâs established curriculum. OPT is not intended to fulfill the requirements of a studentâs program of study and successful program completion does not require participation in OPT; it is optional. In contrast, CPT fulfills an integral element of an established curriculum and successful completion is contingent on participation in CPT.Can CPT be offered as a part of an elective course?In any instance where an elective course is optional, making the CPT optional, the integral and required aspects of CPT would not be met. CPT is an integral part of an established curriculum and the practical training is required for all students participating in that curriculum, regardless of citizenship.Because CPT is allowed only where the training is an integral part of an established curriculum, does that mean that all students enrolled in the established curriculum must participate in and complete practical training?Yes. Unlike OPT, participation in CPT is not optional for any student participating in an established curriculum that the school has determined requires CPT as an integral part of the educational experience. This means that all students â foreign and American â are required to participate in practical training if they are enrolled in an established curriculum where practical training is integral.The question-answer part of the memo said that while auditing and investigating schools to ensure compliance, SEVP (Student and Exchange Visitor Program) has noted that some institutions have described CPT as if it is optional practical training and not integral, despite clear regulatory requirements. SEVP has also discovered that some institutions have not required all students enrolled in the same established curriculum to participate in practical training, despite clear regulatory requirements that CPT is permitted only where the practical training is an integral part of an established curriculum.Are foreign students required to proactively request CPT authorization from their DSO?Yes. Foreign students must make an official request for authorization for CPT to their DSO so that the school can confirm that the student is participating in an established curriculum where practical training is integral, make a determination that the training is directly related to the studentâs major area of study, and update the studentâs SEVIS record to ensure that DHS can conduct proper oversight as required under federal law.Must all CPT be conducted by sponsoring employers that have established cooperative agreements with the school?Yes. Schools should only enter into cooperative agreements with legitimate, bona fide employers who are able to provide a quality practical training experience to students. CPT students should have access to practical training managed by an employer who has entered into a cooperative agreement with a school where it is agreed the employer will sponsor the schoolâs students for specific training such as an alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education or any other type of required internship or practicum that is specific to the studentâs major area of study. Students are not expected to obtain EADs for this training which is an integral and required part of the curriculum.Immigration attorney Emily Neumann said this is not how CPT is used by universities. "When an agency needs a second, three-page broadcast just 12 days later to explain what the first one meant, that tells you the first one raised some serious questions," Neumann wrote.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Iran, Oman discuss temporary shipping lane through Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Omani FM hopes the two countries will ‘soon announce’ a joint temporary transit corridor through the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
Iran and Oman's top diplomats have discussed a proposed framework for a temporary transit corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and a mine-clearing project in the key waterway, which they both border.

Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi arrived in Tehran on Tuesday for talks with his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, to discuss future plans for the strait.

The two "discussed a phased framework that could provide a practical and implementable basis for moving forward", they said in a joint statement shared by Oman.

The strait became a flashpoint early in the Middle East war, and the two countries have recently sought to hammer out a plan to regulate transit through it, as laid out in a June US-Iran memorandum of understanding aimed at ending the war.

"The proposed framework includes the establishment of a temporary joint navigation corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines," the statement said.

"Technical negotiations between the two sides will also continue with the aim of reaching an agreement on a permanent navigation corridor and future arrangements for managing the Strait, alongside establishing a mechanism for exchanging information, managing navigation traffic, and providing related navigational and security services," it added.

Albusaidi said in a post on X after the meeting that he hoped the countries would "soon announce" the temporary corridor in the strait.

"Future management of the strait and a permanent solution will follow in due course," he said.

During their meeting, the two ministers also stressed the importance of reaching arrangements that respect the sovereignty of their respective countries, according to the joint statement.

The diplomats "affirmed the importance of holding joint discussions with the Gulf littoral [coastal] states" to ensure that any agreement reached adheres to international law and respects the sovereignty of neighbouring countries.

The statement came after US President Donald Trump said on his social platform Truth Social that "all mines have been removed and/or detonated from within the International Waters of the Strait of Hormuz", citing the US navy.

"Iran has been notified that any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed," Trump added.

War broke out after the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, with Tehran quickly blockading the Strait of Hormuz and Washington imposing a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

Traffic remains largely paralysed, disrupting global oil markets in a crucial waterway that normally carries around one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas exports.

Iran and Oman, both coastal nations on the strait, have for weeks been discussing the future of navigation through the waterway, with Tehran saying the geographical coordinates of a route envisaged by the two countries "have been agreed upon".

Iranian officials, however, have insisted that the strait will not fully reopen until the US meets Tehran's demands, including lifting its naval blockade, dropping oil sanctions and unfreezing its assets abroad.

articles.title: Damascus condemns Israel Katz after visit with IDF soldiers on Mount Hermon
articles.summary: Katz's visit follows an IDF strike in Syria near Damascus on Saturday, which itself followed a larger strike on a military airfield on August 18. The Syrian...
articles.body:
Katz's visit follows an IDF strike in Syria near Damascus on Saturday, which itself followed a larger strike on a military airfield on August 18.

The Syrian government condemned Defense Minister Israel Katz's visit to Mount Hermon on Tuesday, Syria's Foreign Affairs Ministry said in an X/Twitter post, calling the action "illegal."

"The Foreign Affairs Ministry stresses that these hostile practices constitute a blatant provocation and a clear violation of international law and the United Nations Charter, as well as a breach of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, which requires respect for the ceasefire lines and not crossing them," the ministry's statement read.

The ministry called upon the international community to pressure Israel into stopping its "repeated violations," withdrawing from the territory, and "respecting the sovereignty and territorial unity of the Syria."

Katz met with IDF soldiers based on Mount Hermon during his visit earlier on Tuesday, telling them that Israel "will not move from Mount Hermon and the security zone as long as there are jihadist threats to the State of Israel," according to i24 News.

"The message to the Syrian president is clear," said Katz. "When you wake up in the morning in the palace in Damascus and look up at Mount Hermon and see the IDF, you know that we are here to protect our communities and our border."

Katz emphasized the strategic significance of the territory, noting the vantage point it provides to the IDF along several fronts.

"[It overlooks] Damascus from above, 35 kilometers away, overlooking the Bekaa Valley in Lebanon, a Hezbollah stronghold from above," he was cited by i24 as saying.

IDF strikes Syrian terrorist near Damascus, military airfield in Idlib

Katz's visit follows an IDF strike in Syria near Damascus on Saturday against a terrorist in the "final stages" of preparing a terror attack against Israeli soldiers, the military said at the time.

A more significant IDF strike occured on August 18 against the Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province in northwestern Syria, with experts telling The Jerusalem Post on Wednesday that the strike sought to avoid a direct clash with Turkey amid a buildup of Turkish forces in the area.

Danielle Greyman-Kennard contributed to this report.

articles.title: Diego Pavia Makes Shocking U-Turn After Vanderbilt's Surprise QB Decision
articles.summary: Vanderbilt made a surprise move.
articles.body:
Diego Pavia just weighed in on Vanderbilt's quarterback decision. The former Commodores star backed the coaching staff. He applauded the choice of Blaze Berlowitz as the Week 1 starter.

College football reporter Pete Thamel shared the news on X, adding that Austin Peay will welcome the program's new starting quarterback.

Five-star freshman Jared Curtis will begin the season on the bench. Some might have expected the highly touted recruit to win the job immediately. Pavia took a different view.

He posted strong support for Berlowitz on social media.

"WELL EARNED- been watching this king from the start of time at NM STATE when he took over in the championship game at 18 years old and BALLED," Pavia wrote. "yall better stand down this man the truth!"

Berlowitz spent the last two seasons backing up Pavia. The two first teamed up at New Mexico State. Pavia knows exactly what his former teammate brings to the field.

He sees the decision as earned rather than a slight against Curtis. Berlowitz waited his turn and stayed ready. Pavia wants fans to respect that process.

Curtis remains a major talent. Pavia personally helped recruit the Nashville native to Vanderbilt. The former Heisman runner-up still believes in the freshman's future.

Pavia made clear his support is not a dig at Curtis. He simply celebrates a friend finally getting his shot. The senior has prepared for this moment across multiple seasons.

Vanderbilt opens against Austin Peay on September 5. Berlowitz will take the first snaps. Curtis will continue developing behind him. Pavia stands nearly alone in public approval of the call.

Diego Pavia continues to show loyalty to the program he helped transform. His message remains simple. Stand down and respect the player who earned the job.

articles.title: âIâm not a victimâ: Cinna breaks down after reaching a huge Twitch milestone and opens up about the pressure affecting her mental health
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Brittany âCinnaâ Watts became emotional during her Cinnathon stream after reaching around 80,000 active Twitch subscribers on August 24. The milestone.
articles.body: Brittany âCinnaâ Watts became emotional during her Cinnathon stream after reaching around 80,000 active Twitch subscribers on August 24. The milestone made her the most-subscribed female streamer at the time, based on active subscribers. Instead of simply celebrating, Cinna opened up about how the pressure around her work has affected her mental health. She thanked viewers and her cameraman, Rosii, for standing by her. The achievement followed weeks of growth.Brittany âCinnaâ Watts opens up after reaching 80,000 Twitch subscribersCinna reached the milestone during Cinnathon, her August streaming event that has kept her live through much of August. TwitchTrackerâs August 24 figures listed 79,231 active subscribers, including 75,191 paid active subscribers. TwitchTracker also showed 79,231 as her all-time high.A Cinnathon tracker recorded more than 75,000 new subscribers since August 1, taking her from about 5,000 subscribers at the start of the event to more than 80,000 by August 24.During the event, Cinna gained more than 100,000 Twitch followers, showing that the subscriber record was not the only sign of growth. TwitchMetrics reported an average of about 8,800 viewers across her streams during the 30-day period.On day 24, she said the attention and pressure had been affecting her mental health.âObviously, Iâm a human. Itâs ****ing with my mental health a lot, but the thing that makes it great is you guys, and I just want to say thank you so much.âShe then began crying and spoke about her work. Cinna also gave credit to Rosii, who has worked with her during Cinnathon.âI think that I put in a lot of work into everything that I try to do. I know Rosii puts in a lot of work, and I think I am in a constant state ofâ¦ I feel like Iâm constantly being discredited all the time, and just **** on. Iâm not a victim. I live a good life.âCinna reminds viewers that content creators are human tooCinna then widened the message to other streamers. She asked viewers to remember that creators also deal with pressure away from their numbers.âJust remember that content creators are human too, bro. And weâre all just doing our best. At the end of the day, as long as I know that Iâm a good person, and I do good things, and I do what Iâm supposed to do, then, you know, **** everybody else and what they say, and I appreciate you guys for always being so kind.âShe then tried to lighten the mood, joking about crying and saying, âI hate crying. Cuzâ I look like Jason,â referring to CORE Boys member Jasontheween.The Cinnathon numbers show the support Cinna has received. TwitchTracker currently lists her with more than 79,000 active subscribers, while other tracking data shows strong follower growth during August. TwitchMetrics reported more than 109,000 new followers over the 30-day period ending August 24.For Cinna, the stream was about more than a subscriber number. She used the moment to thank the people supporting her while being honest about how difficult it feels to have her work questioned.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: No intention to quit politics, Nitin Gadkari clarifies
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkariâs office said on Tuesday that his remark that the younger generation should be given more responsibil.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkariâs office said on Tuesday that his remark that the younger generation should be given more responsibility as âhe could no longer take on as much work as beforeâ, had been misinterpreted to suggest that he intended to quit politics.In a statement clearly prompted by speculation triggered by the ministerâs comment on Sunday, his office emphasised that Gadkariâs remarks were âspecifically about the Laxmanrao Mankar Trustâ, an organisation established by him that runs Ekal Vidyalayas in tribal areas.Statement taken out of context, not political: Gadkariâs officeNitin Gadkariâs office said, âIn that context, Gadkari said that he could no longer take on as much work as before and that the younger generation should be given an opportunity to take greater responsibility. His remarks were clearly related to the functioning and future leadership of the Trust. However, some television channels are presenting the statement as a political remark, taking it out of its actual context.âAt an event in Nagpur on Sunday, Nitin Gadkari had said that he has been in active public life for over three decades and during his political journey, he has experienced many ups and downs, fulfilled various responsibilities, and received many honours.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US lawmakers urge Trump team to free American student held by Israel
articles.summary: Congress members call on Marco Rubio to ‘use every tool’ at his disposal to secure release of 20-year-old Sama Safi.
articles.body:
More than 40 members of the United States Congress have penned a letter to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling on him to push for the release of Sama Safi, a 20-year-old US citizen who has been detained by the Israeli military since June.

The legislators warned on Tuesday that the Palestinian American student's health is deteriorating "under appalling conditions" in Israeli custody.

"Every day that Sama remains wrongfully detained in these inhumane conditions, she is at greater risk of irreversible and life-threatening repercussions," the lawmakers, led by Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib , wrote to Rubio.

"Her life is at risk on your watch. We urge you to act swiftly and use every tool at your disposal to secure the immediate release of Sama Safi so that she can receive the medical care she urgently needs and return to her family, her studies, and the life and freedom that every 20-year-old deserves."

Six US senators – including Elizabeth Warren, Bernie Sanders and Chris Van Hollen – signed on to the letter alongside dozens of members of the House of Representatives.

Israeli forces abducted Safi, who was attending Birzeit University, from her home in the occupied West Bank in a predawn raid nearly three months ago, and they have been holding her without charge.

Safi was one of four young women who were detained as part of an Israeli crackdown on anti-occupation activism in June.

Israel has received about $25bn in US military aid since the start of the genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023.

Over the past years, Israeli soldiers and settlers have killed several US citizens, including Sayfollah Musallet , who was beaten to death in a settler attack last year.

In February, Israeli settlers also fatally shot 19-year-old American citizen Nasrallah Abu Siyam. In 2024, the Israeli military killed Aysenur Ezgi Eygi , a US activist from Seattle.

None of the incidents have resulted in criminal charges against the perpetrators.

Israel detained American teenager Mohammed Ibrahim for nine months last year and only released him after an outcry from US lawmakers, as his family warned that the boy may die from malnutrition and mistreatment in Israeli custody.

Rights groups have documented horrific and widespread abuses against Palestinian detainees by Israel, including sexual violence.

"Emergency measures introduced after 7 October 2023 exposed Palestinian detainees to torture, potentially unlawful deaths, incommunicado detention, and degrading conditions," Alice Jill Edwards, the United Nations special rapporteur on torture, said in a report in May.

In their letter to Rubio, the US lawmakers underscored that Safi suffers from a chronic medical condition known as Familial Mediterranean Fever, a genetic disorder that causes fevers and inflammation, but she has not had regular access to her medication.

The Palestinian American detainee has also been moved across several facilities.

"She describes being subjected to repeated verbal abuse and being placed in painful stress positions, as well as the presence of rapidly spreading infectious skin disease, rats, and mattresses reeking of feces," the letter said.

Trump administration 'aware' of the case

The State Department said it does not comment on congressional correspondence, and it declined to comment on the specifics of Safi's case, citing privacy concerns.

A State Department spokesperson told Al Jazeera that the administration of President Donald Trump "has no higher priority than the safety and security" of US citizens.

"We are aware of reports of an American detained in the West Bank," the spokesperson said. "The Trump Administration takes its commitment to assist Americans abroad seriously and we are tracking the situation. When Americans are detained abroad, the Department advocates for their access to adequate medical care, proper treatment, and regular consular visits."

Raed Jarrar, advocacy director at the US-based rights group DAWN, suggested Safi's detention should trigger suspending American military aid to Israel under Washington's regulations, including the Leahy Law.

"Sama Safi is an American citizen. Her own government has abandoned her," he told Al Jazeera. "The State Department's job is to fight for her release, and it is refusing to do that job. US law demands more than advocacy. Under the Foreign Assistance Act and the Leahy Law, prolonged detention without charge is a gross violation of human rights, and Washington must cut all military aid to the Israeli units responsible for holding her."

The Israeli government did not respond to Al Jazeera's request for comment by the time of publication.

Earlier this month, the Israeli military told Florida radio station WMNF that it detained four "female suspects" in the West Bank "after promoting hostile terrorist activity and additional terrorist-related activities".

articles.title: Does 'rewilded' land need better wildfire prevention measures?
articles.summary: RSPB is considering measures it can take to improve resilience in the wake of a five week long fire
articles.body:
As we're driving in a pickup truck to see the aftermath of a huge fire which burnt for more than a month in the Cairngorms, I spot fresh smoke coming from the ground.

My guide - RSPB Scotland's site manager at the Abernethy nature reserve, Ben Oliver-Jones - puts the vehicle in reverse and we jump out to see what's happening.

It's one of several hot-spots which keeps emerging a full week after firefighters left the scene , which Ben likens to a game of whack-a-mole in an already charred landscape where the smell of burning still hangs heavily in the air.

But while the small pockets of smouldering vegetation are still being dealt with, attention is turning to improving wildfire protection.

More than 2,500 hectares of moorland and forest - about 10 square miles - was destroyed in the fire, which led to the evacuation of an entire village and where the smoke could be seen and smelt 60 miles (96.5km) away in Aberdeen.

Like a growing number of Scotland's estates, the Loch Garten and Abernethy nature reserve is being managed for ecological restoration - what others might describe as 'rewilding', a now polarising term which the RSPB avoids using.

Opponents have argued that the process leaves areas more vulnerable to uncontrollable fires, which the charity disputes, but it has identified significant land management changes it plans to make.

The changes focus on four key areas: fire breaks, wetlands, heather management and tree planting.

While the estate's network of tracks functioned as a fire break in some locations, in other areas strong winds helped high flames jump the gap.

Experts say fire from burning heather can reach heights of six metres and that fire breaks need to be three times the flame height.

RSPB Scotland says it now acknowledges that fire breaks need to be wider and has already started that process on its long network of forest trails.

Machines have been used to remove vegetation on either side of the track with the hope that what remains would not create such high flames if it were to ignite.

While it might look desolate now, the hope is that some insects and plant species will eventually colonise the ground either sides of the tracks.

It also plans to create more ponds and wet areas around the site which can be used as a source of water to pump onto fires.

A small fire on the reserve in June was extinguished using water from a pond created with cash from the Scottish government's nature restoration fund as a habitat for species like rare dragonflies.

The charity says it's working to raise water tables where bogs have been drained and create new areas of standing water for fire fighting.

Peatlands have proved problematic for wildfires because the fire can spread through the peat, deep underground as well as on the surface.

It's a problem for degraded peatland which makes up about 80% of Scotland's total, but for those in a near-natural state the peat can act as a defence.

In good condition, they keep the water level high, bringing moisture to the landscape.

Its effectiveness was demonstrated during a large fire near Melvich, Sutherland, in 2019 which reached an area that had been re-wetted 20 years earlier.

Roxane Anderson from the University of the Highlands and Islands (UNI) studied the land before and after the fire and says any damage to wet peatland was superficial and on the surface.

She argues that's a reason for accelerating peatland restoration which is currently targeting 400,000 hectares - about 1,500 square miles - by 2040 and describes it as "a complete no brainer."

"We should do it as much as we can, as quickly as we can and as strategically as we can, especially in the context of this changing climate."

On Monday, Scotland's chief fire officer published an open letter calling for better wildlife planning and urging a "more formal and proportionate fire safety regime" to match that for businesses in urban settings.

It comes as the Scottish government enters the final stages of introducing licences for muirburn - the controlled burning of heather on moorland primarily managed for grouse shooting.

Ministers have brought in the licences to make moorland more "environmentally sustainable", but Scottish Land and Estates say the practice is a valuable tool for reducing vegetation which can act as fuel to a wildfire.

RSPB Scotland does not practice muirburn but accepts that the "fuel load" does need to be managed.

It has been doing that through grazing cattle, which eat the vegetation, while in other areas land managers have used machines to cut and mulch the grass, gorse, bracken and heather.

While some sporting estates remain opposed to "rewilding", others have embraced some of the elements of ecological restoration.

The Rottal estate in the Angus Glens has been working with the RSPB for several years now and owner Dee Ward believes there is a lot of common ground.

He has been re-wetting peatland, planting trees and encouraging wading birds and says that while the "ideological extremists" have been holding the narrative, a lot more estates are trying to find the middle ground.

He added: "There are people that are very anti-grouse shooting. Fair enough, that's your choice. But that's clouding their view about muirburn because they're saying because grouse shooters do it, it must be bad."

Dee urges both sides to begin looking at land management practices through the lens of preventing wildfires and consider sharing appropriate methods.

The fourth move RSPB Scotland plans is the introduction of more broadleaved trees in its woodlands.

It says that while pines contain flammable resins, species such as alder, rowan, aspen and birch are higher in moisture content which means they do not burn as easily.

Abernethy hosts the largest and most important remnant of Scotland's ancient Caledonian pine forest and so the Scots pines are an important part of the mix.

But the charity wants to explore the option of increasing the proportion of other species, which would have occurred naturally in the original forest anyway.

Michael Bruce, owner of the Glen Tannar estate in Aberdeenshire, specialises in controlled burning of moorland and helps the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service with its wildfire forecasting.

He says that there hasn't been enough academic research and modelling in the UK on how wildfires behave to make land management changes meaningful.

While two significant studies have been carried out in Scotland over the past 25 years, neither has been long-term or consistent and he believes events of the summer demonstrate the need for improved understanding.

He believes there is no silver bullet which will prevent a wildfire starting or spreading but that estates "need to build up layers of defence".

Firms affected by Cairngorms wildfire offered support from Â£3m fund Published 6 August

Firms affected by Cairngorms wildfire offered support from Â£3m fund

'Apocalyptic' damage as Cairngorms wildfire burns for two weeks Published 29 July

'Apocalyptic' damage as Cairngorms wildfire burns for two weeks

In April, the Cairngorms National Park Authority introduced a bylaw making it illegal to start a fire or a BBQ during the summer months to prevent wildfires.

Despite the huge blaze, figures suggest that move has been effective at reducing potential sources of ignition, with the number of campfires or barbecues recorded so far this year totalling 36 compared with 94 in the same period last year.

That's still too many but the reduction perhaps emphasises the importance of preventing a fire's spread.

Wildfires have been described to me as an "intermittent problem" because they're seasonal and we don't see large ones happening every year.

If they happened every year, it would become an obvious priority.

Preventing and tackling them both cost money and there are obvious questions around striking the balance between spending on both, not to mention wider affordability.

But climate change is predicted to bring more long, dry spells which create the tinderbox of summer 2026 and so all of this may be seen as an investment in the future.

For five weeks, land managers with very opposing views on how the uplands should be managed stood side by side battling the enormous blaze which was sweeping through the Cairngorms.

They found a common purpose and it's hoped that now seeing the countryside through a prism of wildfire risk may now be the unifier which sees them exchanging at least some practices - even if their end goals for the landscape still differ wildly.

A small fire on the reserve in June was extinguished using water from a pond created with cash from the Scottish government's nature restoration fund as a habitat for species like rare dragonflies.
The charity says it's working to raise water tables where bogs have been drained and create new areas of standing water for fire fighting.
Peatlands have proved problematic for wildfires because the fire can spread through the peat, deep underground as well as on the surface.
It's a problem for degraded peatland which makes up about 80% of Scotland's total, but for those in a near-natural state the peat can act as a defence.
In good condition, they keep the water level high, bringing moisture to the landscape.
Its effectiveness was demonstrated during a large fire near Melvich, Sutherland, in 2019 which reached an area that had been re-wetted 20 years earlier.
Roxane Anderson from the University of the Highlands and Islands (UNI) studied the land before and after the fire and says any damage to wet peatland was superficial and on the surface.
She argues that's a reason for accelerating peatland restoration which is currently targeting 400,000 hectares - about 1,500 square miles - by 2040 and describes it as "a complete no brainer."
"We should do it as much as we can, as quickly as we can and as strategically as we can, especially in the context of this changing climate."

On Monday, Scotland's chief fire officer published an open letter calling for better wildlife planning and urging a "more formal and proportionate fire safety regime" to match that for businesses in urban settings.
It comes as the Scottish government enters the final stages of introducing licences for muirburn - the controlled burning of heather on moorland primarily managed for grouse shooting.

Ministers have brought in the licences to make moorland more "environmentally sustainable", but Scottish Land and Estates say the practice is a valuable tool for reducing vegetation which can act as fuel to a wildfire.
RSPB Scotland does not practice muirburn but accepts that the "fuel load" does need to be managed.
It has been doing that through grazing cattle, which eat the vegetation, while in other areas land managers have used machines to cut and mulch the grass, gorse, bracken and heather.
While some sporting estates remain opposed to "rewilding", others have embraced some of the elements of ecological restoration.
The Rottal estate in the Angus Glens has been working with the RSPB for several years now and owner Dee Ward believes there is a lot of common ground.

He has been re-wetting peatland, planting trees and encouraging wading birds and says that while the "ideological extremists" have been holding the narrative, a lot more estates are trying to find the middle ground.

He added: "There are people that are very anti-grouse shooting. Fair enough, that's your choice. But that's clouding their view about muirburn because they're saying because grouse shooters do it, it must be bad."
Dee urges both sides to begin looking at land management practices through the lens of preventing wildfires and consider sharing appropriate methods.
The fourth move RSPB Scotland plans is the introduction of more broadleaved trees in its woodlands.
It says that while pines contain flammable resins, species such as alder, rowan, aspen and birch are higher in moisture content which means they do not burn as easily.
Abernethy hosts the largest and most important remnant of Scotland's ancient Caledonian pine forest and so the Scots pines are an important part of the mix.
But the charity wants to explore the option of increasing the proportion of other species, which would have occurred naturally in the original forest anyway.
Michael Bruce, owner of the Glen Tannar estate in Aberdeenshire, specialises in controlled burning of moorland and helps the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service with its wildfire forecasting.
He says that there hasn't been enough academic research and modelling in the UK on how wildfires behave to make land management changes meaningful.

While two significant studies have been carried out in Scotland over the past 25 years, neither has been long-term or consistent and he believes events of the summer demonstrate the need for improved understanding.
He believes there is no silver bullet which will prevent a wildfire starting or spreading but that estates "need to build up layers of defence".
Firms affected by Cairngorms wildfire offered support from Â£3m fund Published 6 August
Firms affected by Cairngorms wildfire offered support from Â£3m fund
'Apocalyptic' damage as Cairngorms wildfire burns for two weeks Published 29 July
'Apocalyptic' damage as Cairngorms wildfire burns for two weeks
In April, the Cairngorms National Park Authority introduced a bylaw making it illegal to start a fire or a BBQ during the summer months to prevent wildfires.

Despite the huge blaze, figures suggest that move has been effective at reducing potential sources of ignition, with the number of campfires or barbecues recorded so far this year totalling 36 compared with 94 in the same period last year.
That's still too many but the reduction perhaps emphasises the importance of preventing a fire's spread.
Wildfires have been described to me as an "intermittent problem" because they're seasonal and we don't see large ones happening every year.
If they happened every year, it would become an obvious priority.
Preventing and tackling them both cost money and there are obvious questions around striking the balance between spending on both, not to mention wider affordability.
But climate change is predicted to bring more long, dry spells which create the tinderbox of summer 2026 and so all of this may be seen as an investment in the future.
For five weeks, land managers with very opposing views on how the uplands should be managed stood side by side battling the enormous blaze which was sweeping through the Cairngorms.

They found a common purpose and it's hoped that now seeing the countryside through a prism of wildfire risk may now be the unifier which sees them exchanging at least some practices - even if their end goals for the landscape still differ wildly.

articles.title: Fake Bank Call Convinced Her to Open Her Safe. Police Say a Man Drove Off With $1.5 Million in Jewelry and Metals
articles.summary: A phone call from people posing as bank employees ended with a stranger driving into a Florida woman’s garage and leaving with approximately $1.5 million......
articles.body:
A phone call from people posing as bank employees ended with a stranger driving into a Florida woman's garage and leaving with approximately $1.5 million in jewelry and precious metals from her safe, according to police.

Treasure Island investigators say the scammers first convinced the older resident that her bank accounts and credit cards had been compromised. She wired approximately $280,000 before a bank employee recognized a second attempted transfer as suspicious and stopped it.

Police say the callers then changed tactics. They warned the woman that employees at her own bank could come to her home armed and steal her valuables, then offered a supposed way to protect them.

The six-month investigation has resulted in the arrests of James Arthur Graves Graham Jr., 24, and Alnesha Bianca Handy, 35, while authorities continue trying to identify other participants and locate missing property, according to National Jeweler .

The Callers Posed as Chase and Bank of America Employees

Treasure Island police responded to the woman's home on Feb. 10 after a report involving fraud, grand theft and burglary. Police Chief John Barkley said the callers claimed to represent Chase and Bank of America. When an actual bank employee stopped another large wire transfer, the people on the phone did not end the conversation.

FOX 13 reported that the callers instead convinced the woman that employees at her own bank were involved in the supposed criminal activity. Police say the woman remained on the phone for more than four and a half hours as the callers used fear and urgency to keep her following instructions. She eventually told them that her valuables were stored in a safe in her garage.

The callers instructed the woman to open the safe and garage door and then go back inside the house so she would not see the person supposedly coming to secure her valuables. Police say a vehicle entered the garage and the door was closed. The person inside emptied the safe and drove away with approximately $1.5 million in jewelry and precious metals.

License Plate Cameras and Fingerprints Led Police to Graham

Neighborhood surveillance and Treasure Island's Flock license plate reader system helped investigators narrow a description of the vehicle to a specific truck.

Police identified Graham as the person they believe went to the residence. He reported the vehicle stolen the following day, and investigators later recovered it in the Fort Lauderdale area.

Authorities said surveillance footage and latent fingerprints provided additional evidence. Treasure Island detectives then worked with Tampa police to search Graham's apartment, where investigators say they found clothing consistent with what the person at the victim's home had been wearing. Graham was arrested on one count of first-degree grand theft and one count of second-degree burglary.

The Wire Transfer Led Investigators to Georgia

Detectives and investigators with the Sixth Judicial Circuit State Attorney's Office spent months following financial records and leads through Tampa, Miami, Fort Lauderdale, Georgia, California and Texas. Investigators eventually traced part of the victim's wire transfer to a Georgia account they say belonged to Handy.

The Tampa Bay Times reported that the account, held under the name Handy Helping Hands LLC, contained $114,000 from the original transfer when investigators traced it.

Treasure Island investigators traveled to Georgia and interviewed Handy before the DeKalb County Sheriff's Office arrested her. Police said she faces a grand theft charge.

Police Recovered More Than 83% of the Wire Money

Investigators recovered more than 83% of the approximately $280,000 transferred electronically and returned it to the victim. Barkley described that level of recovery as highly unusual because fraud proceeds are often moved rapidly through multiple accounts and can become difficult to trace. Authorities believe the case may involve a larger fraud network, and additional arrests remain possible.

A Bank Will Not Send Someone to Your Home to Protect Your Valuables

An unexpected caller claiming a bank account has been compromised should be independently verified before any money or property is moved. Treasure Island police advise customers to hang up and call their financial institution using a trusted number, such as the one printed on the back of a bank card.

Banks will not instruct customers to hand jewelry, cash, gold or other valuables to a courier for safekeeping. They also will not require customers to move money to another account simply to protect it from fraud.

If someone claims a courier or representative is already on the way to a home, do not open the door or surrender property. Contact local law enforcement and the financial institution independently.

Anyone who has already sent a wire should notify the originating bank immediately and ask whether the transfer can be recalled or frozen. Acting quickly matters because stolen funds can move through additional accounts within hours.

articles.title: 5-foot red-tailed boa constrictor found crossing rural road in Canada
articles.summary: Boas are known "escape artists," able to slip through surprisingly small gaps.
articles.body:
A 5-foot red-tailed boa constrictor found crossing a rural road in Ontario left everyone wondering where exactly it came from.

According to GuelphToday , Katherine Leonard, senior manager of community services at the Guelph Humane Society (GHS), said the humane society received a call from a resident after a large snake was seen on the road in Arthur near Eliza Street and Wells Street.

Before that call reached staff, another person in the community had already secured the animal in a large plastic container with duct tape, which was how it arrived at GHS.

The humane society does not usually handle animal control in the Arthur area, but staff still assisted in this special instance and pulled an old enclosure from storage, specifically saved for this type of situation.

During intake, Leonard said, the boa showed no immediate signs of illness or injury and appeared to be a fully grown adult measuring just over 5 feet long.

She added that the snake likely had not been outdoors for long and had "been previously cared for," indicating captivity rather than a wild animal encounter.

VCA Canada says red-tailed boas — also called common boas — are nonvenomous snakes from Central and South America that can grow to about 13 feet and often live 20 to 30 years. They are also strong climbers and require tall, secure enclosures in captivity.

Leonard said the humane society does occasionally receive surrendered ball pythons, but a snake of this size is unusual. "It's definitely one of the larger snakes we've seen here," she said.

Leonard noted that boas are known "escape artists," able to slip through surprisingly small gaps in doors, windows, and even ceiling tiles. She said another possible explanation is that the snake may have been dumped by someone who could no longer afford or handle its care.

Large snakes require space, specialized housing, and a long-term commitment — all of which can create serious challenges for owners and rescue organizations.

The snake is being held under the humane society's standard impound process. Leonard said the shelter will keep it through the required five-day period, after which it could be made available for adoption if no owner comes forward.

The shelter is also asking people who are missing a snake — or who know of one that has gone missing — to contact GHS.

Animals that can live for decades and require specialized habitats can quickly become difficult to care for when their needs are underestimated. When that happens, the consequences reach beyond a single household, affecting neighbors, rescuers, and the animal itself.

"It was crossing the road, so it's very fortunate it didn't succumb to any injuries," Leonard said. "Our hope with any animal is always to reunite it with its owner, but, in the event that it doesn't, that's what we're here for."

articles.title: Why Klay Thompson chose to sign with Heat, Coach Erik Spoelstra amid NBA offseason suitors
articles.summary: Klay Thompson had a very specific reason for choosing the Heat led by Coach Erik Spoelstra and Giannis Antetokounmpo.
articles.body:
Why Klay Thompson chose to sign with Heat, Coach Erik Spoelstra amid NBA offseason suitors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

When an NBA player reaches the twilight of their career, they know it, and an instinct to go after the Larry O'Brien trophy kicks in. Klay Thompson feels that exact feeling right now. After two seasons with the Dallas Mavericks , he decided to join forces with the Miami Heat led by Giannis Antetokounmpo and Coach Erik Spoelstra. Why exactly did he make that call? It all came down to adding another ring to his resume.

Thompson explains decision to join Heat led by Antetokounmpo and Spoelstra.

It is no secret that Klay Thompson found his perfect match with the Heat. When Giannis Antetokounmpo is on the floor, teams typically build a wall to prevent him from scoring in the paint. How does Coach Erik Spoelstra solve this problem? Shooters.

The Heat are no stranger to this conundrum. Coach Spoelstra experienced the same situation with LeBron James . Back then, they got Shane Battier , Mike Miller, Mario Chalmers , James Jones and Ray Allen . Now, they'll do the same with Antetokounmpo after Thompson arrives.

This schematic and rotation fit makes so much sense for the Heat . In fact, Thompson posits that his aim really is to hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy once again. If it means he has to play that specific role for Coach Spoelstra and Antetokounmpo, he would gladly do it.

He even outlined other reasons for joining the Heat in his introductory press conference.

"Just the opportunity to play high-level basketball throughout the season and the chance to make a deep postseason run. Those things were so attractive to me. Obviously, you want to maximize your potential as an athlete. I've tasted winning before; there's really nothing like it. Even just getting there and failing is better than not having a shot at it... Looking at the roster, it looked like a great fit as far as me being able to space the floor," Thompson declared.

Thompson couldn't compete to his full potential after the Warriors ' 2022 NBA Championship run. Stephen Curry and the Warriors couldn't make it over the hump again, despite certain acquisitions. When he moved to the Mavericks, they tanked for Cooper Flagg in one season. During his last run with them, it was also clear it was a developmental year to define their identity.

This time around, Thompson will be surrounded by other veteran stars who have been craving a Larry O'Brien trophy. All he has to do is start knocking down shots, spacing the floor, and playing tighter defense if he wants that fifth ring to land on his finger come 2027. Can he help the Heat while breaking out of his shell?

Heat, Giannis Antetokounmpo snubbed in ESPN's Eastern Conference contenders list

Jeff Teague sees the Miami Heat as a better contender than the Philadelphia 76ers

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani’s Return to the Mound Imminent
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani is one step closer to pitching in a live game. Manager Dave Roberts said today that Ohtani will throw to hitters or th...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers ' Shohei Ohtani is one step closer to pitching in a live game. Manager Dave Roberts said today that Ohtani will throw to hitters or throw another bullpen session before possibly pitching Sunday in Detroit against the Tigers, according to Jack Harris of The California Post.

Ohtani has been limited to his designated hitter role for a month as he has dealt with a recurring knee injury. The sore knee, which has bothered him on and off over his career, kept him from participating in this year's All-Star Game. Baseball's unicorn received an injection of some sort during the Break. He was noticeably limping during his time on the field prior to the shot.

The Dodgers have been careful to manage the superstar's workload this season. Even giving him a night off from his DH duties now and again to minimize wear and tear. However, there is a little more than a month to go in the regular season; Los Angeles wants Ohtani to do his part on the mound during the postseason.

It is no secret that Ohtani posts prolific offensive numbers. Currently, he already has 30 home runs and is batting .288 with 80 RBI. It's easy to see why the Dodgers are reluctant to take his bat out of the lineup,

even to rehab his arm. Therefore, he will build up his longevity in Major-League action. His first outing, whether it be Sunday or the next homestand, will only be for one inning.

Los Angeles is hoping that by the time the postseason rolls around, the four-time Most Valuable Player will be able to go at least five innings. It is most likely that Ohtani will be a starting option in October. Los Angeles will not risk losing the DH during the most important games of the season.

Ohtani isn't the only arm on the mend. Tyler Glasnow returns to the mound tonight after missing more than three months with back issues. Glasnow had ace-like stuff before being sidelined. Catcher Will Smith begins a rehab assignment tonight as well. The Dodgers are getting some pieces back at just the right time. Hopefully, they stay healthy.

articles.title: Surrogate, California couple clash in court as newborn fights for life after heart surgery
articles.summary: Nausheen Gilkar told a Dallas court her newborn is suffering after open-heart surgery as the surrogate custody fight with McKenna West intensifies.
articles.body: The critically ill newborn at the center of a bitter surrogate custody fight was placed back on a breathing tube after his condition worsened following open-heart surgery, according to newly filed court documents. The baby is in critical condition and being closely watched at the hospital, intended parents Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed said in filings obtained by TMZ. The couple said the child suffered possible complications after a Norwood procedure, an operation used to treat his severe heart defect, and had to be re-intubated after his condition declined overnight. SURROGATE SAYS BABY 'RIPPED AWAY' 60 SECONDS AFTER BIRTH AS CUSTODY FIGHT ERUPTS AFTER ABORTION REFUSAL In a Dallas courtroom Tuesday, Gilkar and Ahmed faced surrogate McKenna West as they fought over who should make medical decisions for the newborn. The clash has drawn national attention because West says she refused the California couple’s earlier request to terminate the pregnancy after the baby was diagnosed with a life-threatening heart condition. Gilkar and Ahmed call the baby Rumi. West, an Alaska cardiac nurse, calls him Gabriel and is asking a Texas judge to give her sole conservatorship, which would put medical decision-making in her hands. HHS WARNS TEXAS HOSPITALS AGAINST DENYING LIFE-SAVING CARE TO NEWBORN WITH DISABILITY Gilkar told the court the couple has been at their son’s bedside as he fights through treatment. She said that since surgery, he has struggled to breathe, choked on tubes and needed a blood transfusion, according to court reporting by The Associated Press. "He’s our child," Gilkar said, according to the AP. She accused West of trying to take him away. "She’s trying to take him from us," Gilkar said. Gilkar described the newborn as "the love of our lives" and said, "He’s suffering a lot." NEONATOLOGIST SOUNDS ALARM OVER MASSACHUSETTS ABORTION LAW ALLOWING PROCEDURES UP TO BIRTH: 'VERY DISTURBING' The custody feud began after the baby was diagnosed at about 20 weeks with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, or HLHS. West says Gilkar and Ahmed then asked her to terminate the pregnancy. She refused and later traveled to Texas to give birth, Fox News Digital previously reported. HLHS leaves one side of the heart underdeveloped and disrupts normal blood flow. Without treatment, the condition can be fatal within days or weeks, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. AMERICAN RED CROSS DECLARES NATIONAL BLOOD CRISIS AS TYPE O SUPPLY DROPS TO DANGEROUS LEVELS Budner disputes key parts of West’s account and says the couple did agree to the baby’s treatment. He told Fox News Digital that doctors determined on Aug. 14 that the child was eligible for the Norwood procedure, the first of three open-heart surgeries generally used to treat HLHS. Gilkar and Ahmed consented to the surgery, which was performed Aug. 17, he said. At the time, Budner described the baby’s condition as "critical and complex." BOARD-CERTIFIED OBGYN WARNS NEW MASSACHUSETTS LATE-TERM ABORTION LAW EXPOSES MOTHERS TO DANGER West’s lawyers have argued that the court should make sure the baby continues to receive life-saving care. West told the judge she would abandon her custody request if the court determines the intended parents are committed to that care, according to the AP. Gilkar and Ahmed have asked the court to delay a hearing over the temporary restraining order that gave them custody while the legal fight continues, TMZ reported. TWO FAMILIES SUE NORTH DAKOTA HOSPITAL ON ALLEGATIONS BABIES WERE SWITCHED AT BIRTH The custody battle is only one part of the couple’s broader legal fight with West. Before the baby was born, Gilkar and Ahmed filed counterclaims seeking more than $100,000, alleging West breached their surrogacy agreement and caused them emotional distress. The counterclaims, obtained by TMZ, said the couple paid West $60,000 during the pregnancy under an agreement that addressed termination. West has denied wrongdoing and asked the court to dismiss the claims. DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH The dispute has only grown more personal since the baby’s Aug. 12 birth. West said in a New York Post opinion piece last week that she had only about a minute with the newborn, while his umbilical cord was still attached, before he was taken away. A court order has since barred her from seeing or holding the baby. On Tuesday, the judge left that order in place and did not immediately decide the larger question of custody or conservatorship, according to the AP. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton secured an emergency court order before the birth directing that medically necessary care not be delayed or obstructed, Fox News Digital previously reported. Paxton’s office also notified two Dallas medical centers of their obligations to provide life-saving treatment. The Associated Press and Fox News Digital's Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.
